docs.title: Thesis — How streaming models beat batch models, and on what
docs.text:
Purpose: The argument behind the teacher's plan — "take some models that are not streaming and beat them on real metrics." This page states the idea, the established facts it rests on (with sources), the expected course of an experiment, and the results we expect to see. Everything marked illustrative is a pre-registered expectation, to be replaced by measured numbers from the Ch1 run.

Status: Thesis expanded (idea → facts → expected events → expected results). Derivations and estimator definitions to follow in calculation.md.

Formatting note: math is written in Unicode (τ, κ₀, Δκ, ≈, ≥) so it renders identically in Obsidian, GitHub, and the mkdocs site — no LaTeX pipeline required.

docs.title: 1. The idea
docs.text:
On a drifting, unbounded, label-scarce stream, a streaming model with a drift detector returns to pre-drift performance within a bounded number of samples of a concept change, and a batch model does not — because batch models update on a clock, while streaming models update on evidence.

Three scope clauses make the claim precise rather than grandiose:

  1. "Beat" is per-metric, never global. The claim is about the temporal reactivity family — recovery time, detection delay, performance between retrains, memory, label efficiency. It is explicitly not about raw mean accuracy over the whole stream, where a properly tuned, frequently retrained batch model can win (Fact 7 below).
  2. The comparison is fair. Batch baselines get a warm-up window, get retrained, and see the same data in the same order, evaluated under the same prequential protocol. The asymmetry is structural: a batch model's update schedule does not depend on what the data is doing.
  3. The claim is falsifiable. Section 6 lists the observable outcomes that would sink it. If streaming's recovery time is not bounded and smaller than a sane retrain interval, the thesis is wrong.

docs.title: 2. Setting and definitions
docs.text:
Let a stream arrive one sample at a time, and let a concept drift occur at time τ, after which the error rate of every model trained on the old concept rises by Δe. Define:

  • d — detection delay: samples from τ until the drift detector alarms.
  • a — adaptation time: samples from the alarm until the model's rolling performance returns to its pre-drift level.
  • r_next — the next scheduled retrain of a clock-driven batch model (possibly ∞, for a model trained once and never updated).
  • k — the retrain interval of a scheduled batch model.
  • w — the window of the rolling metric (e.g. w = 1000 samples).
  • W — the tolerance window: an alarm within W samples of a true drift counts as a detection with delay; an alarm outside any window counts as a false positive. W is chosen explicitly and justified, per notes/04-evaluation.md.

The recovery time of a model is the number of samples from τ until its rolling performance is back to its pre-drift level.

docs.title: 3. The mechanism
docs.text:
All models are equally good before τ; the difference is what happens after.

  • Frozen batch (train once, deploy, never update): error rises at τ and stays elevated until an external decision to retrain. Recovery time is undefined — the model has no mechanism that reacts to data.
  • Scheduled batch (refit every k samples, no detector): error rises at τ, but the model only watches its clock. If the last retrain was at τ − 1, it stays wrong for almost k more samples; on average it is wrong k/2 samples too long. Recovery time is r_next − τ — luck of phase.
  • Streaming + drift detector: the detector watches the error stream, alarms at τ + d, adaptation starts immediately, and rolling performance is back to baseline at τ + d + a. Recovery time is d + a — bounded and data-driven.

The damage a drift causes is the area under the excess-error curve:

Streaming damage       ≈ (d + a) × Δe
Scheduled-batch damage ≈ (r_next − τ) × Δe
Frozen-batch damage    = unbounded (never recovers on its own)

Streaming wins whenever d + a < r_next − τ — the generic case, since d + a is typically tens to low hundreds of samples while r_next − τ spans the whole retrain interval. That factor, (r_next − τ) / (d + a), is the quantitative content of the project.

docs.title: 4. Facts it is based on (with sources)
docs.text:
# Fact Evidence Source (verified in the vault) F1 Test-then-train prequential evaluation is the accepted streaming protocol; every sample scores before it trains. Batch train/test splits leak future information on temporal data; each sample is used for testing, then training. Gama, Sebastião & Rodrigues (2013), Machine Learning 90:317–346 — notes/04-evaluation.md F2 Drift is detectable online with bounded delay. ADWIN adaptively sizes a window and alarms on significant mean change; DDM tracks error-rate bounds (p ± s: warn at p + 2s, alarm at p + 3s). Bifet & Gavaldà (2009), IDA; Gama et al. (2004), DDM — notes/02-concept-drift.md F3 Adaptive streaming learners recover after drift. ARF: adaptive operators + resampling for abrupt, gradual, recurring drift; HAT: ADWIN per tree node. Gomes et al. (2017), Machine Learning 106:1469–1495; Bifet & Gavaldà (2009) — papers/ F4 Adaptive streaming beats static baselines on real drifting, imbalanced data — with numbers. ROSE: Kappa 63.65 vs next-best 57.85, 24 real imbalanced datasets, 30 ensembles compared. Cano & Krawczyk (2022), Machine Learning 111:2561–2599 — papers/cano-krawczyk-2022-rose.md F5 Detector quality is a three-way trade-off (delay / false alarms / misses); no detector wins all three. KDD '26 framework: 14 detectors × 7 real datasets; defines F1-detection score and normalized detection time. Cerqueira et al. (2026), KDD '26, DOI 10.1145/3770855.3819070 — papers/kdd2026-drift-benchmark.md F6 Label delay/scarcity starves batch retraining; streaming keeps working. STUDD: best label efficiency among non-baseline methods on 19 streams, MDR ≈ 19%. A 10,000-sample label delay shifts detections by ~10,000 samples and pins prequential accuracy below 50%. Delayed labels raise user exposure ~50%, cut detection up to 75%. Cerqueira et al. (2023), Machine Learning 112:4351–4378; Gomes et al. (2022), ACM Comput. Surveys 55(4):75; Botacin & Gomes (2024), Computers & Security 147 — papers/, research/02-delayed-labels.md F7 Counter-evidence: oracle-tuned, frequently retrained batch can beat streaming under delay + rare classes. No-delay benchmark: retrained XGBoost AUC-ROC 92.81 vs ARF 91.02. Delayed-label fraud data: XGBoost AUCPR 23.41 vs ARF 14.23. ARF ~2.2× slower. Amekoe et al. (2024), arXiv:2409.10111 — streaming-vs-batch-metrics.md §3 F8 Comparing many learners across many streams needs Friedman + Nemenyi; single runs are noise. ≥10 seeds, mean ± SD, critical-difference diagrams; Wilcoxon signed-rank for pairs. Demšar (2006), JMLR 7:1–30 — notes/04-evaluation.md

What follows from these facts. F2 + F3 give streaming a bounded reaction time d + a. F4 is literature precedent that adaptive models beat non-adaptive ones on exactly the kind of real data we plan to use. F6 gives the label-scarcity win. F7 is the fence: it defines where we must not claim victory, and it is why the Delay Tax (label delay) is the project's open problem rather than a solved one.

docs.title: 5a. Synthetic streams (ground-truth drift: SEA, Agrawal, Hyperplane, RandomRBF, STAGGER, LED)
docs.text:
A single run (e.g. 100,000 samples, ≥10 seeds) is expected to produce this event sequence; each stage records specific variables:

# Event What happens What we record 1 Warm-up First 20–30% of the stream trains all models; no evaluation (excluded) 2 Steady state Rolling Kappa of adaptive models plateaus near its ceiling baseline level κ₀ (mean over the w samples before drift) 3 Drift onset at τ The generating concept changes; all models' rolling Kappa starts to dip τ is known by construction 4 Detector alarm Streaming detector fires at τ + d; batch models are silent d; whether the alarm falls inside tolerance window W 5 Adaptation Streaming model resets/adapts; rolling Kappa bottoms out, then climbs dip depth; recovery slope 6 Recovery Rolling Kappa re-enters the κ₀ band and stays recovery time d + a 7 (batch) next retrain Scheduled batch refits at r_next, recovering only then; frozen never does r_next − τ 8 Repeat Next drift at the next pre-set position per-drift rows in the summary table

Expected detector behaviour on abrupt synthetic drift (literature-anchored, to be measured): ADWIN alarms within tens of samples, DDM within low hundreds. On gradual drift both slow down — and that slowdown is itself a result (F5's trade-off), not a bug.

docs.title: 5b. Real streams (Elec2, Phishing, Covertype, Airlines, CreditCard)
docs.text:
No ground-truth drift points exist, so the event model changes:

  • Drift is inferred from rolling-metric dips and detector alarms; there is no known τ to measure delay against.
  • Comparison targets post-dip behaviour: dip depth, recovery slope, and the fraction of the post-drift window each model spends below its own baseline.
  • Because Elec2's Kappa+ is known to collapse (protocol caveat), the headline on real data is rolling Cohen Kappa + AUC-PR, with Elec2 secondary.

docs.title: 6. Expected results
docs.text: Everything below is illustrative and pre-registered — plausible values in the ranges the literature (F1–F7) supports, to be confirmed or refuted by the Ch1 run. No number here is a measured result.

docs.title: 6a. The picture we expect: rolling Kappa over time
docs.text:
Schematic (illustrative, not to scale) of one synthetic stream with one drift at τ = 25,000, rolling window w = 1,000:

Figure 1 — the three curves are the whole thesis in one picture: a shallow, short dip that self-heals (streaming, blue); a dip that heals only on the next retrain tick (scheduled batch, orange); a permanent step down (frozen, red). Shaded regions are the damage areas each model pays after the drift.

docs.title: 6b. Illustrative recovery-time numbers (one drift, synthetic stream)
docs.text:
Baseline rolling Kappa κ₀ ≈ 0.85; dip to ≈ 0.5; means over ≥10 seeds (illustrative, not measured):

Model d (delay) Recovery time Rolling Kappa at τ + 1000 Damage area (samples × Δκ) HAT + ADWIN ~40 ~250 ~0.83 ~50 Leveraging Bagging + DDM ~100 ~350 ~0.80 ~90 Scheduled XGBoost (k = 5000) — ~2,400 (phase-dependent) ~0.62 ~900 Frozen RF (warm-up 20%) — never ~0.45 unbounded

The decisive column is damage area: streaming pays ~50–100, scheduled batch pays ~an order of magnitude more, frozen pays forever. Note the scheduled model's recovery time is not a property of the model — rerun with different seed phases and it scatters uniformly over [0, k] (pure phase noise, which the ≥10-seed protocol exposes).

docs.title: 6c. Detector metrics (synthetic, ground-truth)
docs.text:
Detector Expected delay on abrupt drift Expected on gradual drift Trade-off to watch ADWIN tens of samples hundreds–thousands fewer false alarms, slower on gradual DDM low hundreds weak (assumes improving error) fast on abrupt, false alarms on noise Page-Hinkley tens–hundreds moderate threshold-sensitive

Expectation, not a bug: no detector wins delay, false alarms and misses simultaneously (F5). The Ch1 contribution is reporting the trade-off with real numbers and pricing it in damage area — not claiming a magic detector.

docs.title: 6d. Resource metrics (measured; structural expectations)
docs.text:
Metric Streaming (expectation) Batch (expectation) Memory fixed by model size; flat vs stream length frozen: fixed; scheduled: grows with stored window Passes over data 1 ≥1 per refit (scheduled ≈ stream/k passes) Throughput bounded per-sample cost (ARF the expensive one) refit bursts, idle between

Honest losses we expect to report: streaming per-sample cost can exceed batch amortised cost on stationary stretches (ARF ~2.2× per F7); scheduled batch may match streaming rolling accuracy when no drift occurs. The advantage is conditional on change — and we will say so.

docs.title: 6e. The real-data win card (expected direction per claim)
docs.text: Dataset Claim we expect to defend Primary metric Phishing, Airlines streaming rolling Kappa ≥ frozen RF/XGBoost on post-drift windows rolling Kappa Covertype streaming ≥ frozen; scheduled phase noise visible rolling Kappa, damage area CreditCard fraud streaming AUC-PR ≥ frozen; tuned batch reported as upper bound AUC-PR (imbalanced; accuracy meaningless) Elec2 secondary; rolling Kappa + AUC-PR only (Kappa+ collapse caveat) rolling Kappa All datasets Friedman + Nemenyi across datasets; Wilcoxon pairwise; effect sizes critical-difference diagram

docs.title: 6f. What would falsify the thesis
docs.text:
1. Streaming recovery time comparable to or worse than a sane retrain interval (d + a ≥ r_next − τ on average) on synthetic drifts.
  2. Frozen batch's rolling Kappa not dropping at drift — i.e. no real drift, a dataset problem rather than a model win.
  3. No significant difference after Friedman/Nemenyi/Wilcoxon (α = 0.05, ≥10 seeds).
  4. Streaming's resource cost so high that the reactivity win is not worth it (measured and reported, not hidden).
  5. On the no-drift control stream, streaming loses to scheduled batch on rolling accuracy — expected, but it must be shown and explained, not swept under the rug.

docs.title: 7. Protocol and statistics
docs.text: Full experimental protocol (models, datasets, seeds, baselines): see streaming-vs-batch-metrics.md. Statistical design per F8: ≥10 seeds on synthetic; bootstrap windows on real ordered streams; Friedman + Nemenyi across datasets; Wilcoxon signed-rank pairwise; effect sizes. One claim per metric, each with the dataset and number behind it — the win card (§6e) is the deliverable that gets written into Ch1.

docs.title: DF-H: deep hybrid drift detector — ultimate-goal roadmap
docs.text:
Status: approved 2026-11-14 Supersedes: the breadth-first E05–E15 detector roadmap. E01–E17 remain as controls and evidence; the detector track is re-centred on DF-H. Related: docs/Phase0:Research/idea/scope.md §5.3 and §6.5, docs/Reports/Nov14.md, docs/Reports/Results.md, docs/Reports/E17-real-detector-map.md.

Readable summary: Roadmap v2. Evidence snapshot: Nov 14 post-mid-term report.

Status update (2026-11-14): E18 and E19 ran and failed their pre-registered gates (best deep AUC 0.616 vs error 0.598; DF-H 3rd overall, 7.09, behind STEPD/SEED). E20 is not run under the pilot-first rule. E21 now carries the headline: the fixed-delay Lemma-1 synthesis shows label-free Stage 1 warning at 70–513 samples vs 2,120–3,269 for the error-only panel at L = 2,000; the full regimes remain scaffolded. E22 adds the focused capability check: DF-H is 3rd overall (7.34), ahead of HDDM-W, ADWIN, HDDM-A and PageHinkley, behind only SEED/STEPD. See E18, E19, E21 and E22.

docs.title: 0.1 Ultimate goal
docs.text:
Build DF-H, a two-stage drift detector:

  1. Stage 1 — label-free deep monitor. A deep representation model (DriftFormer's encoder, with DeepRiver/an autoencoder as baselines) watches the input stream and emits drift signals without labels: masked-feature SSL loss, embedding shift, head-bank disagreement, predictive entropy.
  2. Stage 2 — supervised confirmation. Classical error-stream detectors (SEED, STEPD, ADWIN, HDDM-A) run on the host's mistakes. A Stage-1 warning is confirmed only when a Stage-2 detector fires inside a short window.
  3. Fusion. A calibrated, pre-registered rule reports both the warning time (Stage 1) and the confirmed detection time (Stage 2).

docs.title: 0.2 Success criteria
docs.text:
Primary — KDD'26 immediate-label benchmark. Same protocol as the current reproduction: 7 datasets × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 50 trials, Hoeffding Tree host, same signal/anchor convention.

Criterion Bar Overall average rank top-2 (currently SEED/STEPD at 2.12) Weak cells best on at least two of feature_permutation, feature_filtering, recurring False alarms FAR no worse than ADWIN Per-dataset robustness no dataset rank worse than 4 Stretch #1 overall, or a clear win on all three weak cells

Secondary — the Delay Tax benchmark (the novel contribution).

Criterion Bar Fixed delay L DF-H warning time grows by ≤ L + c, while error-only detectors are floor-bound at τ + L Partial labels DF-H keeps higher recall than the best error-only detector at p = 0.5 and p = 0.1 Selective labels DF-H warns earlier on unlabelled drift; confirmation still needs labels Lemmas Lemma 1 (floor), Lemma 2 (1/√p), Lemma 3 (batch FAR) verified empirically

Negative result is acceptable. If DF-H does not beat the baselines, the delay-tax measurement and Lemmas 1–3 still stand — the scope already declares this a publishable negative result. The detector track cannot sink the project.

docs.title: 0.3 Non-goals
docs.text:
• Do not optimise DriftFormer as a classifier. E14 shows it is weaker than ARF on real streams (κ 0.524 vs 0.724; damage_ref 284.9 vs 198.0). It is a signal extractor, not the benchmark model.
  • Do not replace the KDD Hoeffding Tree host. A deep host would make the comparison a different benchmark.
  • Do not train a deep model per KDD trial. Use a frozen per-dataset encoder and precompute signals.
  • Do not expand the E05/E08–E13 matrix. Those are deferred.
  • Do not build Chapter 2 (the service) before the detector result.

docs.title: 1. Why this is the right goal
docs.text:
The current evidence points to exactly one missing artefact: a detector that uses information the scalar detectors cannot see.

  • No scalar detector wins everywhere. E04: HDDM-A is best on all four synthetic shapes on the static host, but recurring is only F1 0.500. E17: on real Elec2 the default is host-conditional — HDDM-A wins all four shapes on the static HT, but ADWIN wins abrupt 1.000 vs 0.400 and recurring 0.770 vs 0.593 on the adaptive HAT. The best-host mean is ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910.
  • The external benchmark has headroom but a low ceiling. KDD'26: SEED/STEPD rank 2.12 (mean F1 0.300/0.303); HDDM-W 3.56; HDDM-A 3.87. Absolute F1 is low, so a better signal matters — but naive combinations raise false alarms (E02: EWMA makes ADWIN 0.548/1k and KSWIN 7.667/1k vs a 0.1 target).
  • Feature-space detection is the strongest arm on feature drift. ABCD(X) is cited as rank 1.0 abrupt / 3.3 gradual on feature permutation. A deep representation monitor is a nonlinear version of that idea.
  • The mechanism already exists in DriftFormer. _step() computes a masked-feature SSL loss and feeds an internal ADWIN; forward() returns the four head logits and the cls_out embedding. The detector is an instrumentation and fusion problem, not a new model.
  • The hybrid is already the declared contribution. scope.md §5.3 names "label-free early warning + delayed supervised confirmation" as the headline; §6.5 argues it is the information-maximal architecture. This plan makes it the centre instead of a late chapter.

docs.title: 2. What "based on DeepRiver" means, and the scope amendment
docs.text:
DriftFormer/DeepRiver supplies the representation, not the classifier.

  • KDD benchmark host: Hoeffding Tree (same as the current reproduction). The deep monitor is an additional, label-free detector channel.
  • Synthetic/real validation host: Hoeffding Tree and HAT/ARF, to test host-conditional behaviour.
  • Scope amendment (dated note in scope.md §9): deep models are permitted as label-free signal extractors for the hybrid detector. They are not the benchmark classifier and do not replace the classical baseline. This is the implementation of §6.5, not a reversal of the classical scope.
  • Fallback if deep is disallowed: replace Stage 1 with a classical feature-space monitor (PCA/KS/linear MMD, ABCD(X)-style). The fusion, gates, and delay benchmark are unchanged.

docs.title: 3.1 Stage 1 — label-free deep signals
docs.text:
All signals are computed per window (default 500 samples, stride 100) from a frozen encoder, and normalised against the first 20% of the stream.

Signal Definition Why it should help ssl_loss Masked-feature cross-entropy from the SSL head on the window The encoder's own reconstruction/feature model becomes surprised embedding_shift Standardised L2 distance between window mean/covariance of cls_out and a reference window; optional linear MMD Direct P(X) change; strong on feature permutation/filtering head_disagreement Mean pairwise JS/TV across the four head softmaxes Concept uncertainty without labels entropy Predictive entropy of the active head Confidence collapse internal_adwin Existing ADWIN on the SSL loss Cheapest deep signal; baseline feature_ks Max per-feature KS statistic vs the reference (classical control) Shows how much the deep monitor adds over a simple test

Encoder training. Per dataset, train DriftFormer's encoder with the SSL objective on a fixed un-drifted reference sample (20k rows, or all rows for small datasets). Freeze it. No labels are used for Stage 1. For synthetic streams, train on the first 12k warm-up samples or a separate reference seed.

docs.title: 3.2 Stage 2 — supervised confirmation
docs.text:
Use a fixed panel, not a test-time best-detector oracle:

  • SEED and STEPD — the KDD'26 top two.
  • ADWIN — best on the adaptive host in E17.
  • HDDM-A — best on the static synthetic host in E04.
  • Raw mistake channel only; E02 rules out EWMA.

docs.title: 3.3 Fusion
docs.text:
Pre-register the rule; report all variants as ablations:

Variant Rule S1 Stage 1 only (label-free) S2 Best fixed scalar detector only OR Stage 1 or Stage 2 AND Stage 1 and Stage 2 within W_confirm = 2,000 2of3 Stage 1 + SEED + ADWIN, two of three 2of3_nodeep SEED + ADWIN + HDDM-A, two of three (control)

v1 uses a fixed weighted z-score with a threshold calibrated to FAR ≤ 0.1/1k on E02 and the pre-drift 20% of each trial. v2 replaces the fixed weights with a small logistic regression / gradient-boosted model trained on window features.

Leakage rule. Any learned fusion is trained with leave-one-dataset-out on KDD and never tuned on the test trials. Synthetic streams are training-only.

docs.title: 3.4 Warning vs confirmed alarm
docs.text:
For the delay benchmark, report two times separately:

  • T_warn: first Stage-1 alarm (no labels needed).
  • T_confirm: first Stage-2 confirmation after the label arrives.

This is the honest version of the hybrid: Stage 1 can beat the reaction floor, Stage 2 cannot. Lemma 4 (pure posterior drift) is exactly the case where Stage 1 has no power and Stage 2 must do the work.

docs.title: 4.1 KDD'26 immediate-label benchmark
docs.text:
• Protocol: unchanged from experiments/kdd_bench.py — 7 datasets, 4 drift types, abrupt/gradual, 50 trials, 100k row cap, shuffled per trial, Hoeffding Tree host.
  • Convention: headline uses --signal correct --gradual-anchor code (reproduces the published F1 tables); the paper-protocol defaults are a robustness check.
  • Deep signal path: precompute in the main environment; kdd_env loads .npz signals and runs pure-NumPy fusion. No torch in kdd_env.
  • Baselines: SEED, STEPD, HDDM-A, HDDM-W, ADWIN, DDM, S1, S2, 2of3_nodeep, and the current best 2of3.
  • Metrics: KDD F1, FAR/1k, NDT, average rank over 56 cells, per-drift-type rank, per-dataset rank, Friedman/Nemenyi, bootstrap CIs over trials.
  • ABCD/ABCD(X): keep cited from the paper; do not run the expensive arm.

docs.title: 4.2 Delay Tax benchmark (replaces E15)
docs.text:
• Regimes: fixed L ∈ {0, 10, 100, 1000}; geometric mean L; partial p ∈ {1, 0.5, 0.1}; selective (only flagged samples labelled); batch arrival b ∈ {1, 16, 128}.
  • Hosts: Hoeffding Tree and ARF.
  • Detectors: SEED, STEPD, ADWIN, HDDM-A, DF-H.
  • Metrics: T_warn, T_confirm, FAR, recall, downstream damage/recovery.
  • Lemmas: L1 floor (T ≥ τ + L), L2 power loss (1/√p), L3 batch FAR inflation, L4 identifiability (pure posterior drift).
  • E06 stays as the Lemma-1 pilot; E21 is the full benchmark.

docs.title: 4.3 Controls
docs.text:
• No drift: E02, for FAR calibration.
  • Pure posterior drift: label_swap on unchanged P(X) — Stage 1 must be blind; Stage 2 must catch it.
  • Feature drift: feature_permutation/feature_filtering — Stage 1 should win; Stage 2 may add little.
  • Host swap: HT vs HAT — the E17 host-conditional result must hold.

docs.title: Phase 0 — close the in-flight work (time-boxed)
docs.text:
1. Commit the working tree in logical units; keep the 99 MB ARFF and the JVM crash log out of git.
  2. Finish E03's 11-seed run (20/22 units done); regenerate the summary and schedule report.
  3. Document E14 with acceptance rules; render E17 figures.
  4. Reconcile the E01 74.8/515.0 and E02 FAR numbers across live docs.
  5. Add the new Roadmap v2 page and nav.

Exit: a clean enough tree to start the detector without mixing unrelated changes into its commits.

docs.title: Phase 1 — instrumentation (E18 scaffold)
docs.text:
• DriftFormerLearner.signal_snapshot() returns per-block ssl_loss, head_disagreement, entropy, and cls_out statistics.
  • New DeepSignalMonitor owns the windowing, reference statistics, and normalisation.
  • Artifact writer emits signals.npz beside the existing series.npz.
  • Refactor kdd_bench.py to expose a pure-NumPy build_trial_stream(task, data) used by both the KDD runner and the deep precompute.
  • Tests: shapes, finiteness, determinism, stream parity.

Exit: a 1,500-sample SEA smoke run and a 1-seed E17 run produce finite, deterministic signal arrays.

docs.title: Phase 2 — signal-validation gate (E18)
docs.text:
• Extract signals on SEA, Hyperplane, Elec2, and a KDD pilot: 2 datasets × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials = 80 trials.
  • Measure windowed AUC for "drift within the next W samples" on held-out datasets; compare every deep signal against the raw error-rate baseline.
  • Go/no-go gate: at least one deep signal has AUC ≥ 0.75 on held-out data and beats the error-rate AUC by ≥ 0.10. If not, stop or fall back to the classical feature monitor.

Exit artifact: experiments/results/e18/ + docs/Reports/E18-deep-signals.md.

docs.title: Phase 3 — DF-H v1, rule-based fusion (E19)
docs.text:
• Implement the fusion variants; evaluate on synthetic + E17 + the KDD pilot (2 datasets, 5 trials).
  • Gate: top-2 on the pilot; best on at least one feature cell; FAR ≤ ADWIN; no pilot dataset rank worse than 3.
  • Exit: artifact + report; decide whether v2 is worth the full KDD run.

docs.title: Phase 4 — DF-H v2, learned fusion + full KDD (E20)
docs.text:
• Train the fusion on synthetic + a subset of KDD datasets; leave-one-dataset-out.
  • Full 7 × 4 × 2 × 50 KDD run with precomputed deep signals.
  • Gate: top-2 overall; best on at least two weak cells; FAR ≤ ADWIN; no dataset rank > 4. Stretch: #1 overall.
  • Exit: final KDD artifact + docs/Reports/E20-deep-kdd.md; Results row.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Delay Tax benchmark (E21)
docs.text:
• Add label regimes to the harness: fixed, geometric, partial, selective, batch.
  • Run DF-H vs SEED/STEPD/ADWIN/HDDM-A on the delay regimes.
  • Gate: T_warn ≤ L + c; T_confirm matches the best error-only detector plus the expected label delay; partial/selective recall improvement; Lemma 1–3 slopes measured.
  • Exit: delay artifact + docs/Reports/E21-delay-detector.md; headline contribution.

docs.title: Phase 6 — write-up and minimal system
docs.text:
• Restructure the final report around the detector:
  • Measurement lab + baseline detector map (E01/E02/E04/E17/KDD).
  • DF-H architecture + immediate-label benchmark (E18–E20).
  • Delay Tax benchmark + lemmas (E06/E21).
  • Minimal system/demo or a clearly scoped Chapter 2.
  • The mid-term report stays frozen; corrected numbers go into the final report.

docs.text: Risk Mitigation / fallback Deep signal has no discriminative power Phase-2 gate stops early; fall back to a classical feature monitor (PCA/KS/linear MMD) with the same fusion KDD host mismatch Keep the Hoeffding Tree host; deep model is only a signal channel Leakage in the learned fusion Leave-one-dataset-out; pre-register the rule; no test-trial tuning Deep compute cost Frozen per-dataset encoder; batched GPU inference; cached signals; pilot-first DriftFormer is a weak classifier Never use it as the host; use its encoder only; compare against an autoencoder/DeepRiver representation False alarms Raw channel only; E02-calibrated threshold; confirmation window; FAR target Scope says deep is out Dated scope amendment: deep is a label-free signal extractor, not the benchmark classifier; classical fallback ready Delay floor cannot be beaten Report warning vs confirmed separately; Lemma 1 is a theorem, not a failure KDD protocol quirks Use the public-code convention for the headline; run the paper convention as a robustness check Laptop thermal ceiling Reduced worker counts / taskset; hand heavy runs to the user

docs.title: 10. Assumptions and open decisions
docs.text:
1. "Beat the benchmark" = top-2 overall + best on at least two weak cells. #1 overall is the stretch goal. If #1 is mandatory, tighten Phase-4 gates and add an ABCD-style feature ensemble, but do not promise it.
  2. Deep is allowed as a label-free signal extractor. The benchmark host stays classical. If the teacher forbids deep, use the classical feature-monitor fallback.
  3. Frozen per-dataset encoder, not per-trial training. This keeps the KDD benchmark feasible and the comparison fair.
  4. Pilot-first compute. No full 50-trial deep signal run until the 80-trial pilot passes.
  5. Cut list is accepted. E05, E08–E13 (except the lite ablations) and the full Chapter 2 are deferred.
  6. Heavy commands are handed to the user. Per the project rule, the agent writes and statically checks the scripts; the user runs the long jobs.

If any of these is wrong, the affected phase changes; the architecture and gates do not.

docs.title: 11. Definition of done
docs.text:
• DF-H implemented as a reusable detector adapter with tests.
  • E18 signal report with a clear go/no-go verdict.
  • E19 pilot result; E20 full KDD result with a DF-H row beside SEED/STEPD.
  • E21 delay benchmark with Lemmas 1–3 measured (or a documented negative result).
  • New docs pages wired into mkdocs.yml; Results/progress/scope updated.
  • The mid-term report remains frozen; the final report is written from saved artifacts.
  • One-command reproduction for every result.

docs.text:
Experiment Role after this plan Exp-01 / Exp-02 Legacy pilot; superseded by E01 E01 Corrected metric / control E02 No-drift FAR calibration E03 Baseline ladder; finish, no expansion E04 Synthetic detector map / baseline E06 Lemma-1 delay pilot E07 DriftFormer block gate E14 Real-stream host validation E17 Real-stream detector map / host-conditional baseline KDD'26 External benchmark / baseline ranking E18 Deep signal extraction + validation gate E19 DF-H v1, rule-based fusion, pilot E20 DF-H v2, learned fusion, full KDD E21 Delay Tax detector benchmark + lemmas E05, E08–E13, E15 Deferred/cut except the lite ablations

The single sentence to remember: a deep label-free monitor provides the signal no error-stream detector can see; a supervised confirmation stage keeps the cells where SEED/STEPD are strong; DF-H is the detector that owns both.

docs.title: E01 — Metric v2 correction (Exp-01/02 revision)
docs.text: Status: concluded (clean three-model panel: DeepRiver, frozen RF, timing oracle) · Artifact: experiments/results/e01/ · Command: uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e01

docs.title: 1. Why this experiment exists
docs.text:
Exp-01 and Exp-02 reported a 294× mean damage gap and a 24× worst-vs-best gap. Both were inflated by a defect in the metric, not by the models:

  • damage_area integrated from τ to the recovery point.
  • On 8 of 11 seeds the recovery rule collapsed to recovery = τ (the model never left its band), so the integral covered a single sample.
  • Streaming damage was therefore truncated; frozen damage — which never recovered — was integrated over the full window.
  • Both numbers were upper bounds, and the viva brief already flagged the defect as a known weakness.

E01 re-runs the same pilot with a metric that cannot be gamed this way.

docs.title: 2. What metric v2 changes
docs.text:
Metric Definition Why damage_ref (primary) Σ max(κ_ref − κ(t), 0) over a fixed window from τ κ_ref is shared across the model panel, so a weak model cannot score zero damage by having a low own-baseline damage_full Same, from τ to the end of the stream Prices the whole remaining stream, not just the pre-registered window AUE mean error minus the timing-oracle error over the fixed window Dimensionless; oracle is an RF refit at τ on pre-drift data T_exit / T_recover Recovery only counts after a real band exit Removes the “0 = instant recovery” artefact recovery_rate Fraction of seeds with a real recovery Replaces the misleading mean of a floored recovery time

The fixed window is 5,000 samples for the abrupt SEA stream. The recovery band is 0.95·κ_ref with a 500-sample stretch.

docs.title: 3. Setup
docs.text:
Stream SEA, one continuous U(0,10)³ draw Length 60,000 samples · warm-up 12,000 · drift at τ = 30,000 Drift abrupt: x₀ + x₁ > 8 → x₀ + x₁ > 9 Noise 10% label noise Seeds 11: 42, 0…9 Streaming DeepRiver RollingClassifier, RNN 3→16→2, window 500 Frozen RandomForestClassifier(100), fit once on the warm-up Oracle RF refit at τ on the last 12k pre-drift samples (knows when)

The panel is DeepRiver, frozen RF, and the timing oracle. The earlier artifact that also contained HT/HAT — caused by a host-default bug that has since been fixed — is archived at experiments/results/_archive/e01_5model/; every number below comes from the clean rerun.

docs.title: 4.1 Aggregate, 11 seeds
docs.text:
Metric DeepRiver Frozen RF Timing oracle Full-run accuracy 0.8830 ± 0.0021 0.8539 ± 0.0017 0.8543 ± 0.0016 Full-run Cohen κ 0.7530 ± 0.0044 0.6850 ± 0.0035 0.6860 ± 0.0033 AUE −0.0472 ± 0.0058 +0.0010 ± 0.0027 0 (reference) damage_ref (5k window) 74.8 ± 61.8 515.0 ± 97.1 505.0 ± 97.6 damage_full (rest of stream) 321.4 ± 203.8 3,472.9 ± 559.7 3,425.4 ± 506.8 Recovery rate 8/11 (0.727) 0/11 (0.000) 0/11 Recovery time, recovered seeds 285–4,279; mean 1,502 never never

The two panels are deliberately separate: damage_ref is the primary damage metric, AUE is the excess over the timing oracle. AUE is negative for DeepRiver because the timing oracle is weak (its damage_ref is 505, almost identical to frozen), not because DeepRiver is impossible.

docs.title: 4.2 Per-seed damage_ref
docs.text:
Seed DeepRiver Frozen RF 42 51.7 514.2 0 25.1 402.6 1 13.1 498.5 2 46.1 509.5 3 159.6 565.9 4 55.4 522.5 5 80.1 578.2 6 24.8 295.2 7 71.3 586.7 8 77.9 531.9 9 217.9 660.0 mean ± SD 74.8 ± 61.8 515.0 ± 97.1

DeepRiver's damage is lower on 11/11 seeds. With the clean panel the worst DeepRiver seed (217.9) sits below the best frozen seed (295.2) — 0.74× its damage. The mean gap is 6.9×, and the full-stream gap is 10.8×.

docs.title: 5. Verdict
docs.text:
Pre-registered condition Required Measured Verdict Frozen never recovers every seed 0/11 PASS DeepRiver damage_ref lower ≥10/11 seeds 11/11 PASS AUE vs timing oracle ratio or better DeepRiver −0.0472, frozen +0.0010 PASS — mechanism, not upper bound

The claim survives; the magnitude shrinks. A streaming model that keeps learning pays about 6.9× less damage in the pre-registered window than a frozen model (10.8× over the rest of the stream), and the frozen model never recovers. The old 294× and 24× are retired.

docs.title: 6. What this retires
docs.text:
• 294× mean damage gap → corrected to 6.9× (damage_ref) or 10.8× (damage_full) on the clean panel.
  • 24× worst-vs-best → retired. The worst DeepRiver seed is 0.74× the best frozen seed; the worst-case claim was a truncation artefact. The earlier four-model panel's 1.27× is superseded by the clean rerun.
  • “835 samples” → seed 42 still recovers in 835 samples under the corrected rule, but recovery is 8/11, with values 285–4,279. The number was seed luck; the distribution is the result.
  • “Damage area and dip depth are the trustworthy metrics” → too generous. damage_ref is the trustworthy one; damage_full is the one that prices the whole stream; recovery time is meaningful only conditional on an exit.

docs.title: 7. Caveats to keep in the report
docs.text:
1. Panel composition (resolved). The panel is DeepRiver, frozen RF, and the timing oracle. The pre-fix four-model artifact is kept at experiments/results/_archive/e01_5model/ for auditability; the numbers here are the clean rerun and supersede it.
  2. AUE is not an upper bound. The timing oracle knows when the drift happened but is refit only on pre-drift data; its damage is almost identical to frozen. AUE therefore measures “excess over a weak oracle,” not “distance from the best possible model.” Use damage_ref as primary.
  3. One synthetic stream. This is still SEA, one abrupt drift. The detector matrix, real streams, and the Delay Tax are the next gates.

docs.title: 8. Reproduce
docs.text:
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e01
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e01 --report
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e01 --figure-only

Artifacts: experiments/results/e01/summary.json, experiments/results/e01/models.jsonl, experiments/results/e01/episodes.jsonl, experiments/results/e01/series.npz.

docs.title: E04 — Which drift detector works for which drift shape?
docs.text: Status: first pass, 5 seeds · Artifact: experiments/results/e04/ · Command: uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e04 --seeds 0-4

docs.title: 1. Question
docs.text:
The project has eight early-warning signals and four kinds of change. Before building a detector into the learning system, we need the map:

  1. Which signal catches which kind of change?
  2. How quickly does it ring?
  3. How often does it cry wolf when nothing changed?
  4. Does the answer depend on the learner whose mistakes are being watched?

This is the detector half of the project. E01 measured recovery; E04 measures whether the system can notice that recovery is needed.

docs.title: 2. Design
docs.text:
Generators SEA, Hyperplane, RandomRBF, Agrawal Shapes abrupt, gradual, incremental, recurring Length 60,000 samples · warm-up 12,000 · change at τ = 30,000 Seeds 5: 0–4 (first pass; the full matrix uses 11) Hosts static Hoeffding Tree (ht) and adaptive HAT (hat) Detectors ADWIN, KSWIN, PageHinkley, DDM, EDDM, FHDDM, HDDM-A, HDDM-W Channels raw mistake signal, and EWMA-smoothed mistake signal δ_max abrupt 1,000 · gradual 2,000 · incremental 4,000 · recurring 2,000

Each detector watches the host's mistake stream. A detection inside the acceptable window counts as a true positive; an alarm outside any window counts as a false positive. Detection delay is normalized by the per-shape δ_max.

docs.title: 3. The scoring bug we found
docs.text:
The first report selected KSWIN for incremental with F1 = 1.0 but episode recall = 0.25. That is impossible.

The cause: when a detector made zero alarms, precision was None, so its run was excluded from the F1 average, while its zero recall still counted. A detector that almost never rang therefore looked perfect.

The fix: recompute precision, recall and F1 from the raw TP / FP / detected / n_episodes counts, and treat zero alarms as F1 = 0. The fix is in metrics.evaluate_detections; experiments/detector_report.py recomputes the E04 report from detections.jsonl without rerunning the models.

The KSWIN “perfect” result was an artefact. It is not a result.

docs.title: 4. Corrected result
docs.text:
HDDM-A on the raw mistake signal is the best cell for every shape. Its best host differs: static HT for abrupt, adaptive HAT for gradual/incremental/ recurring.

Drift shape Best default Balanced score Changes caught Alarm precision False alarms /1k Detection delay Abrupt HDDM-A, raw 0.683 75% 0.650 0.0075 0.185 Gradual HDDM-A, raw 0.842 95% 0.796 0.0083 0.155 Incremental HDDM-A, raw 0.883 90% 0.871 0.0033 0.012 Recurring HDDM-A, raw 0.500 73% 0.404 0.0308 0.144

Balanced score = harmonic mean of alarm precision and episode recall. It is a stricter, false-alarm-aware score than plain recall; it is not the KDD paper's exact F1 (which counts multiple alarms per episode), so compare it within this table, not against KDD tables.

docs.title: 5. Findings
docs.text:
1. HDDM-A raw is a sensible default on the static host and these synthetic generators. It wins all four shapes, keeps false alarms below 0.031 per 1,000 examples, and catches 73–95% of changes. The real-stream follow-up (E17) shows this does not transfer to the adaptive host — see §8.
  2. Recurring change is the hard case. Its best balanced score is 0.50 with 40% alarm precision: it rings often enough to catch changes, but also rings when the stream has only switched back to a concept it has seen before.
  3. Incremental change is the easiest. HDDM-A reaches 0.883 with 0.003 false alarms per 1,000 and a detection delay of 0.012 of the allowed window.
  4. Gradual was not harder than abrupt in this slice. HDDM-A scores 0.842 on gradual vs 0.683 on abrupt, and most detectors have a lower normalized delay on gradual. This contradicts the usual “gradual is harder” expectation. Treat it as a first-pass finding, not a law: per-shape δ_max, the longer transition window, and the balanced score all affect the comparison.
  5. Smoothing is not free. On the smoothed channel, KSWIN produces 5.4–7.5 false alarms per 1,000 examples and ADWIN 0.4–0.6; their balanced scores collapse. The raw signal is the default; the smoothed signal is a diagnostic. This matches the no-drift control (E02).
  6. Detector rankings are mostly host-stable. For raw channels, the HT-vs-HAT rank correlation is 0.8–1.0 for most detectors; KSWIN is the exception at 0.4. The delay changes with host, but the ordering usually does not. We do not claim a uniform “adaptive learners hide drift” effect from this slice.

docs.title: 6. What this does not say
docs.text:
• It is a 5-seed first pass, not the pre-registered 11-seed matrix.
  • It uses default detector settings; no tuning. E05/S06 are for that.
  • It is synthetic only; no real streams, no label delay. A first real-stream check is E17 (one dataset, one injected mechanism), not a full external-validity test.
  • The balanced score uses episode recall, not the KDD benchmark's multi-alarm recall. Raw counts are in detections.jsonl if a different definition is needed.
  • The E04 config has no acceptance rule, so the committed artifact's "pass": true is vacuous. Do not quote it as a pass. The harness now reports pass: null with an explicit "nothing was asserted" note for empty acceptance blocks; the committed E04 artifact predates that fix.

docs.title: 7. Reproduce
docs.text:
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e04 --seeds 0-4
uv run python -m experiments.detector_report
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e04 --figure-only

Artifacts: experiments/results/e04/summary.json, experiments/results/e04/detections.jsonl (raw counts), experiments/results/e04/detector_report.json (corrected report), experiments/results/e04/figures/.

docs.title: 8. Follow-up — E17 on real Elec2 (2026-11-13)
docs.text:
The synthetic default is host-conditional on real data. Eight detectors were replayed on 45,312 real Elec2 records, shuffled per seed, with a known label-swap drift injected at τ = 22,656; five seeds, the same two hosts.

Drift shape HDDM-A, static HT ADWIN, static HT HDDM-A, adaptive HAT ADWIN, adaptive HAT Abrupt 0.933 0.452 0.400 1.000 Gradual 0.960 0.495 1.000 1.000 Incremental 0.960 0.842 1.000 0.971 Recurring 0.787 0.508 0.593 0.770

On the static Hoeffding Tree, HDDM-A repeats the four-shape win. On the adaptive HAT it does not: ADWIN wins abrupt and recurring, ties gradual, and loses only incremental. The best-host mean F1 is ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910. The one-sided Hoeffding test can miss an abrupt change that the adaptive learner repairs quickly; ADWIN's two-sided window comparison still sees it. Recurring remains the hard case.

Five seeds, one dataset and one injected mechanism: this is a warning about the scope of the E04 claim, not a final ranking. Full write-up: E17-real-detector-map.md.

docs.title: E14 — real-stream model comparison (5-seed slice)
docs.text:
Status: provisional conclusion, 2026-11-14. Artifact: experiments/results/e14/. Role after Roadmap v2: host validation only — DriftFormer is a signal extractor for DF-H, not the benchmark classifier.

Scope guard. Two real datasets, five seeds, one injected mechanism per stream. The acceptance rules below were written after the first slice; they set the bar for the expansion and are evaluated provisionally here. This page does not license a field-wide ranking.

docs.title: 1. The question
docs.text:
Exp-01/02, E01, E04 and E17 are synthetic or single-dataset checks. E14 asks the external-validity question: does the streaming advantage survive real features and real labels, and is the deep model a viable host on real streams?

The answer matters twice for DF-H:

  • if streaming adaptation survives real data, the delay-tax benchmark has a credible host;
  • if the deep model does not beat ARF as a classifier, it should be used only as a label-free signal extractor — which is the design choice in Roadmap v2.

docs.title: 2. Design
docs.text:
Datasets Elec2 (45,312 rows) and Phishing (1,250 rows), shuffled per seed Drift injected at a known position: label_swap and feature_permutation, abrupt Models frozen RF, ARF, HAT, DriftFormer, oracle refit Seeds 0–4 Runs 100 model runs, 100 episodes Protocol prequential test-then-train, shared warm-up, metric v2 (damage_ref, damage_full, Cohen κ, recovery)

The oracle refit is a timing oracle only: it knows when the drift happened but not what the new concept is, so it is a weak upper bound.

docs.title: Pooled over 20 dataset × mechanism × seed cells
docs.text:
Model Accuracy Cohen κ damage_ref damage_full Recovery rate Frozen RF 0.685 0.395 297.4 4,703.0 0.00 ARF 0.875 0.724 198.0 2,684.8 0.20 HAT 0.803 0.583 245.7 3,019.6 0.15 DriftFormer 0.770 0.524 284.9 3,497.5 0.00 Oracle refit 0.698 0.415 280.3 4,518.3 0.00

E14 pooled over Elec2 + Phishing, five seeds. ARF pays the least damage; the oracle's damage is almost identical to frozen, which is why AUE is a secondary metric.

docs.title: By dataset
docs.text:
Dataset Model damage_ref Cohen κ Recovery rate Elec2 ARF 202.4 0.666 0.00 Elec2 HAT 268.3 0.593 0.00 Elec2 Frozen RF 295.0 0.392 0.00 Elec2 DriftFormer 314.7 0.545 0.00 Phishing ARF 193.5 0.782 0.40 Phishing HAT 223.0 0.573 0.30 Phishing DriftFormer 255.2 0.503 0.00 Phishing Frozen RF 299.8 0.397 0.00

Reading. ARF leads on both real datasets: lowest damage_ref, highest κ, and the only meaningful recovery. HAT is second. DriftFormer beats frozen on κ but not on damage — on Elec2 it pays slightly more than frozen (314.7 vs 295.0). Real-stream drift is harder than SEA: recovery rates are low everywhere.

docs.title: 4. Acceptance rules and provisional verdict
docs.text:
These rules are recorded here, not in e14_real_streams.yaml: changing the registry's acceptance block changes the config hash and would invalidate the committed cache. They will move into the registry when E14 is expanded and rerun.

Rule Bar Measured (20 cells) Verdict A1 — pooled damage ARF damage_ref ≤ 0.75× frozen 0.666× (198.0 / 297.4) PASS A2 — per-cell robustness ARF lower damage_ref in ≥ 16/20 stream × seed cells 18/20 PASS A3 — frozen never recovers frozen recovery rate = 0 on every cell 0/20 PASS A4 — full-run skill ARF κ ≥ frozen κ + 0.10 +0.329 (0.724 vs 0.395) PASS

Provisional verdict: PASS on all four rules. The streaming advantage survives the first real-stream check. The magnitude is not transferable to a field-wide claim: the slice has two datasets, five seeds, one injected mechanism per stream, and Phishing has only 1,250 rows.

Acceptance is about ARF, not DriftFormer. The question is whether streaming adaptation survives real data, so the pre-registered comparison is ARF vs frozen. DriftFormer's weaker classifier result is a separate, expected negative: it is the evidence for using the deep model as a signal extractor in DF-H, not as the KDD host.

docs.title: 5. What this changes
docs.text:
• E14 is concluded as a provisional slice, not as a field-wide result.
  • DriftFormer is not the benchmark host. Roadmap v2 already uses its encoder only; E14 is the measured justification.
  • No statistical ranking across datasets. With two datasets and five seeds, a Friedman/Nemenyi claim is not available. Expansion to ≥5 datasets and ≥10 seeds is deferred under Roadmap v2; E14 remains host validation.
  • The numbers here supersede the provisional table in Nov 14 §4.6 only in status, not in values.

docs.title: 6. Reproduction
docs.text:
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e14

Artifacts: summary.json (pooled), episodes.jsonl (per-cell), models.jsonl, series.npz, figures/. The five-seed slice is committed; a full rerun is a heavy command and is handed to the user per the project rule.

docs.title: E17 — The detector map on a real stream (Elec2)
docs.text: Status: first real-stream pass, 5 seeds · Artifact: experiments/results/e17/ · Command: uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e17 --seeds 0-4

docs.title: 1. Question
docs.text:
E04 found HDDM-A on the raw mistake signal to be the best cell for every one of the four synthetic drift shapes. That was a synthetic-only result: the streams came from SEA, Hyperplane, RandomRBF and Agrawal. Does the default survive when the error stream comes from real records?

This is a detector check, not the E14 model check. It asks whether the eight alarms still rank the same way when the features and labels are real.

docs.title: 2. Design
docs.text:
Stream River Elec2 — 45,312 real electricity-market records, 8 features, binary label Drift label swap 0 → 1 injected at a known position Shapes abrupt, gradual, incremental, recurring Length 45,312 · warm-up 9,062 · change at τ = 22,656 Widths abrupt 0 · gradual 2,000 · incremental 10,000 · recurring period 8,000, 2 episodes Seeds 5: 0–4 Hosts static Hoeffding Tree (ht) and adaptive HAT (hat) Detectors ADWIN, KSWIN, PageHinkley, DDM, EDDM, FHDDM, HDDM-A, HDDM-W Channels raw mistake signal, and EWMA-smoothed mistake signal δ_max abrupt 1,000 · gradual 2,000 · incremental 4,000 · recurring 2,000

Rows are shuffled per seed, then the label swap is injected. Shuffling removes Elec2's natural temporal drift, so the only known change is the injected one. This is the semi-synthetic protocol of the KDD'26 benchmark, not a natural-drift test: it preserves real feature complexity and class overlap while keeping exact detection ground truth.

An alarm inside [τ, τ_end + δ_max] is a true positive; an alarm outside any window is a false alarm. f1 is the project's balanced score, the harmonic mean of alarm precision and episode recall. Zero-alarm runs count as F1 = 0. FAR is false alarms per 1,000 samples. NDT is the delay normalized by the per-shape δ_max, measured from the drift end.

docs.text:
This is a descriptive summary, not a pre-registered ranking: the host and channel for each detector are chosen after seeing the means.

Detector Best host / channel Mean F1 over the four shapes ADWIN hat / raw 0.935 HDDM-A ht / raw 0.910 PageHinkley hat / raw 0.788 FHDDM hat / raw 0.715 HDDM-W hat / raw 0.580 DDM ht / raw 0.573 KSWIN ht / raw 0.506 EDDM ht / raw 0.413

docs.title: 4. Findings
docs.text:
1. On the static host, HDDM-A repeats the synthetic result. It has the best mean F1 in all four shapes: 0.933 abrupt, 0.960 gradual, 0.960 incremental, 0.787 recurring. Its false-alarm rate stays at 0.0044 per 1,000 except for recurring, where it is 0.0265.
  2. On the adaptive host, the default breaks. ADWIN wins abrupt (1.000 vs 0.400) and recurring (0.770 vs 0.593), ties gradual at 1.000, and loses only incremental (0.971 vs 1.000).
  3. The failure is the one-sided test meeting a self-repairing learner. HDDM-A only alarms when the error rate rises significantly above its frozen low-error reference. HAT adapts on its own, so an abrupt label swap can be repaired before the cumulative test separates. ADWIN compares two windows two-sidedly and still sees the distribution change. This is the concrete version of E04's caution that the host changes what a detector sees.
  4. Recurring change remains the hard case. HDDM-A's precision on the static host is 0.667; on the adaptive host its recall falls to 0.70. ADWIN catches all recurring episodes on both hosts but pays 0.031–0.128 false alarms per 1,000.
  5. Raw still beats EWMA. Every best cell in §3c uses the raw channel; no smoothed cell wins a shape. This agrees with E04 and the E02 no-drift control.
  6. Do not claim a new overall winner. The best-host mean is ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910. The honest statement is: HDDM-A is the best default on the static host; ADWIN matches or beats it on the adaptive host.

docs.title: 5. What this does not say
docs.text:
• It is one real dataset, one injected mechanism (label swap 0 → 1), and 5 seeds. It is not the KDD'26 seven-dataset, four-mechanism, fifty-trial benchmark.
  • The rows are shuffled, so natural temporal drift is removed. This tests detector response to a known injected change, not natural drift in Elec2.
  • Elec2 is binary and comparatively easy; several cells are near-perfect, which compresses the differences between detectors.
  • The label-swap direction interacts with one-sided detectors. A drift that lowers the error rate would be invisible to HDDM-A by construction.

docs.title: 6. Reproduce
docs.text:
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e17 --seeds 0-4
uv run python -m experiments.detector_report --exp e17
uv run python -m experiments.run --exp e17 --figure-only

Artifacts: experiments/results/e17/summary.json, experiments/results/e17/detections.jsonl (raw counts), experiments/results/e17/detector_report.json (corrected report), experiments/results/e17/figures/. Config: experiments/registry/e17_real_detector_map.yaml.

docs.title: 7. Next — the KDD'26 benchmark reproduction
docs.text:
The KDD'26 paper benchmarks 14 detectors on 7 real datasets and reports SEED, STEPD and ABCD as the strongest overall; HDDM-A is mid-tier. A first real-stream check on one dataset cannot settle that. The isolated parallel runner experiments/kdd_bench.py reproduces the paper's Monte Carlo protocol:

  • one task = one (dataset, drift type, transition, trial) run;
  • the Hoeffding Tree is trained once and all detectors are updated in the same pass, avoiding the public code's per-detector learner re-runs;
  • 13 detector configurations: 11 scalar detectors, ABCD on the error stream, and ABCD(X) on the feature vector;
  • 50 trials per cell by default, with --resume;
  • four drift mechanisms and abrupt/gradual transitions.

Status (2026-11-13): the isolated environment resolves, check constructs all 13 configurations in both modes, and the six-detector benchmark has now run at both 10 and 50 trials on all 7 datasets, with the public-code-exact settings (--signal correct --gradual-anchor code).

Detector 10-trial rank 50-trial rank 50-trial mean F1 SEED 2.23 2.12 0.300 STEPD 2.30 2.12 0.303 HDDM-W 3.56 3.56 0.163 HDDM-A 3.94 3.87 0.155 DDM 4.52 4.54 0.101 ADWIN 4.45 4.80 0.122

The 50-trial run confirms the 10-trial ranking. SEED and STEPD tie at 2.12; HDDM-A is fourth at 3.87, behind HDDM-W (3.56). The paper-protocol defaults (--signal error, --gradual-anchor paper) gave the same top two and the same mid-tier HDDM-A rank (3.91), so the conclusion is robust to the convention.

The absolute F1 values reproduce the paper's Tables 5–6 for the shared detectors. Abrupt feature permutation: SEED/STEPD/HDDM-A/HDDM-W = 0.572/0.526/0.313/0.237 here vs 0.61/0.53/0.36/0.25 published. Gradual feature permutation: 0.424/0.442/0.089/0.122 vs 0.46/0.45/0.10/0.14. DDM's abrupt feature-permutation F1 is 0.021 vs 0.02 published. Not every cell matches (ADWIN's class-prior and filtering F1 are lower here), but the six-detector ranking is clear. The published tables therefore appear to use the public code's correctness signal and onset-anchored gradual window, not the paper's Algorithm 1 error signal.

The ABCD/ABCD(X) arm was not re-run. It is the most expensive part of the matrix, it overheats the 16-thread laptop CPU, and it is not needed for the HDDM-A conclusion. The paper's published result is used for that cell: ABCD(X) is the strongest detector on feature permutation (average rank 1.0 abrupt / 3.3 gradual). Treat the ABCD row as cited, not reproduced.

uv sync --project experiments/kdd_env
./experiments/kdd.sh prepare --download-usp
./experiments/kdd.sh check

# headline six-detector comparison (50 trials, all 7 datasets)
./experiments/kdd.sh run --datasets all --trials 50 --workers 14 \
    --signal correct --gradual-anchor code \
    --detectors ADWIN,DDM,HDDMAverage,HDDMWeighted,SEED,STEPD \
    --out experiments/results/kdd_bench_full

# ABCD/ABCD(X) is not re-run: it is the expensive part of the matrix and
# overheats the laptop CPU. The paper's published values are used for that cell.

The runner is deliberately explicit about two public-code discrepancies: the released code feeds correctness (int(true == pred)) into MOA detectors that document 1 = error, and its gradual window is (onset, onset) rather than the paper's end-anchored window. The script defaults follow the paper (--signal error, --gradual-anchor paper); the headline run above uses --signal correct --gradual-anchor code because that configuration reproduces the published F1 tables.

docs.title: E18 — the deep signal gate
docs.text:
Status: concluded, 2026-11-14. Artifacts: experiments/results/e18/ (summary.json, detection.json, detection.csv) · experiments/data/deep_signals/pilot/ (80 trial files). Role: Stage-1 signal validation for DF-H. Gate result is negative.

The one-line verdict: the deep signals have real timing value on feature drift, but they do not clear the pre-registered AUC gate, and a simple feature_ks control is often just as good. The deep encoder's marginal value is unproven.

docs.title: 1. What was tested
docs.text:
E18 asks whether a frozen, label-free DriftFormer encoder produces signals that predict drift better than the raw error rate. The pilot is 2 datasets × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials = 80 cells:

Datasets Covtype (54 features), Electricity (8 features) Drift class_prior, label_swap, feature_permutation, feature_filtering Transitions abrupt, gradual Trials 5 per cell; KDD protocol, 100k-row cap, seed 12 Encoder DriftFormer, SSL-only pretraining on 20k fixed unlabeled rows per dataset Windows 500 samples, stride 100, reference = first 20% of windows Signals ssl_loss, embedding_shift, embedding_var_shift, head_disagreement, entropy, internal_adwin, feature_ks Baseline River Hoeffding Tree prequential error rate on the same trial

The report label is a causal detection window: a window is positive if it overlaps the drift or ends within one window of its end. The plan's “drift in the next W” wording would ask the monitor to predict a future change; a causal monitor cannot do that, so the report uses the detection label. This correction is documented in experiments/deep_kdd.py.

docs.title: 2. Primary gate — FAIL
docs.text:
The pre-registered gate was: at least one deep signal with AUC ≥ 0.75 and ≥ 0.10 above the error-rate baseline. Measured over all 80 cells:

Signal AUC vs error feature_ks (classical control) 0.628 +0.029 embedding_shift 0.616 +0.017 embedding_var_shift 0.599 +0.000 error_rate 0.598 — ssl_loss 0.532 −0.067 head_disagreement 0.530 −0.069 internal_adwin 0.501 −0.098 entropy 0.471 −0.128

Gate result: FAIL. Best deep signal 0.616, short of 0.75 and only +0.017 over the error rate. Even the classical feature_ks control misses the bar.

E18 — the deep signals cluster around the error-rate baseline overall. The right panel shows where the signal actually lives: feature permutation, where embedding_var_shift reaches 0.781, but the error rate is stronger still (0.879). Label-only drift is correctly left to Stage 2.

docs.title: Where the signal lives
docs.text:
Drift type Best signal AUC Error-rate AUC feature_permutation embedding_var_shift 0.781 0.879 feature_filtering feature_ks 0.651 ~0.50 class_prior feature_ks 0.622 ~0.50 label_swap error_rate 0.698 —

The deep signal does have power on feature permutation (0.781), but the error rate is stronger there (0.879). On label-only drift (label_swap), the deep signal is correctly near chance (0.51) while the error rate catches it (0.698) — Stage 2's job.

docs.title: 3. Secondary diagnostic — timing at a controlled FAR
docs.text:
AUC is not how a detector operates. The deep_kdd detect command calibrates each signal on pre-drift windows to 0.1 false alarms/1k, then measures the first alarm after onset. Key feature-drift cells:

Cell Signal Hit rate Median delay FAR/1k Covtype feature-permutation, abrupt ssl_loss 100% 72 0.09 Covtype feature-permutation, abrupt error_rate 100% 184 0.04 Covtype feature-permutation, gradual ssl_loss 100% 244 0.05 Covtype feature-permutation, gradual error_rate 100% 1,033 0.13 Electricity feature-permutation, abrupt ssl_loss 100% 83 0.06 Electricity feature-permutation, abrupt error_rate 80% 198 0.07 Electricity feature-permutation, gradual embedding_var_shift 100% 214 0.15 Electricity feature-permutation, gradual error_rate 80% 864 0.13 Electricity feature-filtering, abrupt embedding_shift 100% 350 0.16 Electricity feature-filtering, abrupt error_rate 0% — 0.09 Electricity feature-filtering, gradual feature_ks 100% 1,176 0.04 Electricity feature-filtering, gradual error_rate 0% — 0.14

E18 timing — lower is better. SSL loss and embedding var shift alarm well before the error rate on feature permutation. On feature filtering the error rate misses entirely while the feature signals still fire. “miss” means no alarm inside the 2,500-sample budget; percentages mark hit rates below 100%.

Reading. Stage 1 detects feature permutation 2–5× earlier than the error rate, and detects feature filtering when the error rate is blind. On label-only drift it stays quiet at this FAR, which is what Stage 2 is for.

The catch. feature_ks is often as fast as the deep signals (84 vs 72 on Covtype abrupt permutation; 350 vs 350 on Electricity abrupt filtering), and sometimes faster. The deep encoder is not clearly adding information beyond a simple per-feature KS monitor. That is the risk the E19 ablation was built to test.

docs.title: 4. What this changes
docs.text:
• The AUC gate is a negative result and stays recorded as such.
  • The deep signals are not a standalone detector; they are a warning channel with real timing value on feature drift.
  • The classical feature_ks control must travel with the deep signals into E19. If the deep view does not beat it there, the classical monitor is the honest Stage 1.
  • No full 50-trial E20 run is justified by this gate alone. E19 pilots the fusion; the result decides whether E20 is worth the compute.

docs.title: 5. Reproduce
docs.text:
uv run python -m experiments.deep_kdd report \
    --signals experiments/data/deep_signals/pilot \
    --out experiments/results/e18

uv run python -m experiments.deep_kdd detect \
    --signals experiments/data/deep_signals/pilot \
    --out experiments/results/e18 --far 0.1 --budget 2500

# figures in this page
uv run python experiments/scripts/make_e18_e19_figures.py

The signal extraction itself is:

uv run python -m experiments.deep_kdd prepare-signals \
    --datasets Covtype,Electricity --trials 5 \
    --out experiments/data/deep_signals/pilot --device cuda

See E19 — DF-H v1 pilot for the fusion result.

docs.title: E19 — DF-H v1 pilot (rule-based fusion)
docs.text:
Status: pilot concluded, 2026-11-14. Gate: FAIL. Artifact: experiments/results/e19_kdd_pilot/. Pre-registration: experiments/registry/e19_hybrid_detector.yaml.

The one-line verdict: DF-H v1 ranks third overall on the 80-cell KDD pilot, behind STEPD and SEED. It owns feature cells in ablation variants, but the primary 2of3_both does not win one, and it is tied fifth on Covtype. The pre-registered top-2 gate fails, so the full E20 run is not justified.

docs.title: 1. Design
docs.text:
The pilot is the plan's 2 datasets × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials = 80 cells, using the KDD'26 protocol and the public-code convention (--signal correct --gradual-anchor code).

Stage 1 — deep max(ssl_loss_z, embedding_shift_z) Stage 1 — classical feature_ks_z (the E18 control) Stage 1 — both max(deep, classical) Stage 2 SEED, STEPD, ADWIN, HDDM-A, HDDM-W Thresholds calibrated on pre-drift windows to 0.1 FAR/1k, per dataset Fusion window 2,000 samples; refractory 2,000 Variants S1_deep, S1_classical, S1_both, OR_deep, AND_deep, 2of3_deep, 2of3_classical, 2of3_both (DFH), 2of3_nodeep (control)

The fusion reports the confirmation time for AND/2-of-3 rules and the earliest alarm for OR. The control 2of3_nodeep uses SEED + ADWIN + HDDM-A, so it isolates the feature-monitor contribution.

docs.title: 2. Overall result
docs.text:
Detector Mean F1 FAR/1k Overall rank STEPD 0.281 0.05 5.22 SEED 0.267 0.06 5.44 DFH = 2of3_both 0.223 0.04 7.09 2of3_deep 0.221 0.04 7.12 2of3_classical 0.220 0.04 7.75 HDDM-W 0.170 0.28 7.31 OR_deep 0.178 0.15 7.72 S1_both 0.160 0.13 8.50 AND_deep 0.201 0.01 8.53 S1_deep 0.144 0.12 8.81 S1_classical 0.151 0.13 8.84 ADWIN 0.117 0.11 9.59 2of3_nodeep (control) 0.154 0.03 9.97 HDDM-A 0.128 0.04 11.00

DF-H beats the no-feature control by 2.9 ranks (7.09 vs 9.97) and has the lowest FAR among the competitive rows. It does not beat the top scalar detectors.

E19 — left: average rank over the 80 cells; DFH is third, behind STEPD and SEED. Right: mean F1 against mean false alarms. DFH sits below the top two in F1 but has the lowest FAR of the competitive rows; AND_deep is the low-FAR outlier, but its overall rank is 8.53.

docs.title: 3. Gate check
docs.text:
Criterion Bar Measured Verdict Overall rank top-2 DFH 3rd (7.09; STEPD 5.22, SEED 5.44) FAIL Weak feature cells best on ≥1 of feature permutation/filtering DFH wins none; AND_deep wins abrupt permutation (1.50), S1_both wins gradual filtering (1.00) FAIL for primary; ablations pass False alarms FAR ≤ ADWIN 0.04 vs 0.11 PASS Per-dataset robustness no rank worse than 3 Covtype tied 5th–7th (avg pos 6.0; rank 7.44), Electricity tied 3rd–4th (avg pos 3.5; 6.75) FAIL (strict bar)

docs.text:
Cell Best detector Rank DFH rank Abrupt feature permutation AND_deep 1.50 5.75 Gradual feature permutation STEPD 1.00 5.50 Abrupt feature filtering OR_deep 2.75 11.00 Gradual feature filtering S1_both 1.00 9.25

The feature monitor does own feature cells in ablation form. The problem is the primary 2-of-3 rule: it asks for Stage-2 confirmation on cells where Stage 1 is already right and Stage 2 is slow or blind (feature filtering), and it leaks Stage-1 false alarms on label-only cells where Stage 1 has no power.

docs.title: 4. What this changes
docs.text:
• Do not run the full 7 × 4 × 2 × 50 E20 matrix. The pilot-first rule says the gate must pass first; it did not.
  • The deep view does not earn a clear place over the classical control. 2of3_both (7.09), 2of3_deep (7.12) and 2of3_classical (7.75) are close; feature_ks was often just as fast in E18. The honest Stage 1 for a v2 is the classical feature monitor, with the deep view as an ablation.
  • The warning/confirmation idea still works where it should. AND_deep is the best detector on abrupt feature permutation (rank 1.50, FAR 0.01), and Stage 1 is correctly blind to label-only drift. The failure is the fixed 2-of-3 rule, not the information.
  • Covtype robustness is the weak point. DFH is tied 5th–7th there, driven by label-only cells where the feature monitor has no power and the 2-of-3 rule still waits for it.
  • A v2 is only worth it with a gating hypothesis: activate Stage 1 only when a feature-drift confidence is high, and defer to Stage 2 on label-only cells. That needs more than two datasets for leave-one-dataset-out; the current pilot cannot validate a learned gate.
  • Pivot to E21. The Delay Tax benchmark is the novel contribution and does not require DF-H to win the KDD rank. The lemmas and the delay measurement stand on their own.

docs.title: E21 — the Delay Tax detector benchmark
docs.text:
Status: fixed-delay Lemma-1 headline measured, 2026-11-14. Artifacts: experiments/results/e21/delay_floor.json + .csv; figure docs/Reports/figures/e21-delay-floor.png. Scope: this is a fixed-delay synthesis from the committed E19 trial artifacts. The full stochastic/partial/selective/batch regime matrix is scaffolded (experiments/driftlab/labels.py) but not yet run.

The one-line verdict: a label-free Stage 1 warning does not pay the label tax. At L = 2,000, Stage 1 warns in 70–513 samples after onset while SEED/STEPD need 2,120–2,710 and ADWIN 2,472–3,269.

docs.title: 1. What is being measured
docs.text:
An error-only detector watches the host's mistakes. It cannot react to a drift until the labels for the post-drift samples arrive. Under a fixed delay L, its detection time is therefore floor-bound:

T_error(L) ≥ τ + L

A label-free Stage 1 monitor watches the input stream itself. It has no label floor. That is the Delay Tax: the same drift, seen through the same detector panel, costs L extra samples for every error-only method and nothing for the feature monitor.

This page measures the fixed-delay case on the same 80 KDD cells used by E19. Stage 1 is the label-free S1_deep / S1_classical alarm; the error-only lines are the scalar mdt from the same trials, shifted by L.

docs.title: 2. Result
docs.text:
E21 fixed-delay synthesis. Blue/gray flat lines are label-free Stage 1; dashed red/orange/purple lines are error-only detectors with base + L. The gap is the label tax.

At L = 2,000 samples, detection delay after onset:

Cell Stage 1 deep Stage 1 classical SEED STEPD ADWIN Covtype, abrupt 70 90 2,130 2,120 2,472 Covtype, gradual 306 406 2,710 2,616 — Electricity, abrupt 76 196 2,129 2,180 3,269 Electricity, gradual 293 513 2,701 2,694 —

— means the detector had no detection in that cell. Stage 1 is 4–30× earlier than the error-only panel at this delay. At L = 0 Stage 1 is already earlier in every cell; the gap grows linearly with L.

docs.title: 3. Why this matters
docs.text:
E18 and E19 are negative on their own gates: the deep signal did not beat the error-rate AUC, and DF-H v1 did not reach top-2 on the KDD rank. E21 is the part that survives those negatives.

The value of the feature monitor is not a better average rank. It is that its warning is not floor-bound by label arrival. The error-only detectors are strong on immediate labels (SEED/STEPD are the KDD top two), but they cannot escape τ + L. Stage 1 can.

The honest limit: Stage 1 alone is not a good detector on label-only drift (E18/E19), so the detector still needs Stage 2 confirmation. The result is a warning/confirmation split, not a standalone deep detector:

  • T_warn — Stage 1, label-free, not shifted by L.
  • T_confirm — Stage 2, floor-bound at τ + L.
  • The report should quote both times, never a single blended number.

docs.title: 4. What is implemented, what is not
docs.text:
Implemented and tested:

  • experiments/driftlab/labels.py — fixed, geometric, partial, selective, and batch label-arrival schedules, with deterministic seeds.
  • experiments/tests/test_label_regimes.py — arrival-time and availability invariants.
  • The fixed-delay synthesis and figure in this page.

Not yet run:

  • The full E21 regime matrix (geometric mean delay, partial p ∈ {0.5, 0.1}, selective labels, batch b ∈ {16, 128}).
  • The actual delayed-learning rerun (this synthesis shifts the error-only detection time by L; the full benchmark should train the host on the schedule too).
  • Lemmas 2 (partial-label power loss) and 3 (batch FAR inflation) measured end-to-end.

That remaining work is the difference between the fast headline and a full benchmark. The headline is enough to state the contribution; the matrix is the next extension.

docs.text:
# fixed-delay floor from the committed E19 trial artifacts
uv run python experiments/scripts/make_e21_delay_figure.py

# label schedule tests
uv run pytest experiments/tests/test_label_regimes.py -q

The figure is generated from experiments/results/e19_kdd_pilot/trials.csv and summary.csv; no model rerun. See E18 for the signal artifacts and E19 for the fusion pilot.

docs.title: E22 — detector shootout on the datasets we have
docs.text:
Status: concluded, 2026-11-14. Artifact: experiments/results/e22_detector_shootout/. Question: what is DF-H actually capable of against the classical detectors we care about — ADWIN, HDDM-A, HDDM-W and PageHinkley — on the data already in the repo?

The one-line verdict: DF-H is third overall (7.34), behind only the KDD top two (STEPD 5.44, SEED 5.59), and ahead of every requested classical detector: HDDM-W 7.47, ADWIN 9.94, HDDM-A 11.34, PageHinkley 12.53. It wins feature permutation outright against that panel and has the lowest FAR of the high-F1 rows. It does not beat SEED/STEPD, and feature filtering is better handled by the Stage-1-only ablation.

docs.title: 1. Design
docs.text:
The 80-cell KDD pilot already used for E19, now with the requested classical panel plus the two KDD reference detectors:

Data Covtype (54 features), Electricity (8 features) Cells 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials = 80 Classical panel ADWIN, HDDM-A, HDDM-W, PageHinkley Reference SEED, STEPD (KDD'26 top two) Ours S1_deep, S1_both (label-free Stage 1), DFH = 2of3_both Protocol KDD 100k cap, --signal correct, --gradual-anchor code Stage-1 thresholds pre-drift, 0.1 FAR/1k

The deep signals are the committed E18 artifacts; no new signal extraction was needed. The run is one command and about 90 seconds on 8 workers.

docs.title: 2. Overall result
docs.text:
E22 — left: average rank over 80 cells. Right: mean F1 against mean FAR; top-left is better. DF-H sits below SEED/STEPD in F1 but has the lowest FAR of the high-F1 rows. HDDM-W buys F1 with a much higher false-alarm rate; PageHinkley barely alarms and barely scores.

Detector Mean F1 FAR/1k Overall rank Family STEPD 0.281 0.05 5.44 KDD reference SEED 0.267 0.06 5.59 KDD reference DF-H (ours) 0.223 0.04 7.34 hybrid HDDM-W 0.170 0.28 7.47 requested Stage 1 both 0.160 0.13 8.66 label-free Stage 1 deep 0.144 0.12 9.00 label-free ADWIN 0.117 0.11 9.94 requested HDDM-A 0.128 0.04 11.34 requested PageHinkley 0.018 0.01 12.53 requested

Reading. DF-H beats ADWIN by 2.6 ranks, HDDM-A by 4.0, HDDM-W by 0.13, and PageHinkley by 5.2. It does not beat SEED/STEPD. PageHinkley's 0.01 FAR is not a win: it almost never alarms (F1 0.018).

docs.title: 3. Where the capability lives
docs.text: E22 — left: rank in the four feature cells. Right: mean F1 by drift type. The hybrid is strongest on feature permutation; the Stage-1-only variants own feature filtering; label-only drift is the weak cell.

docs.title: Feature cells
docs.text:
Cell DF-H ADWIN HDDM-A HDDM-W PageHinkley Abrupt feature permutation 5.8 10.5 8.8 11.8 16.0 Gradual feature permutation 5.5 15.5 13.2 13.0 15.5 Abrupt feature filtering 11.5 11.5 11.5 4.0 11.5 Gradual feature filtering 9.2 10.2 10.2 9.5 14.2

On feature permutation, DF-H beats every requested classical detector on both transitions. On feature filtering, HDDM-W wins abrupt and DF-H is only marginally ahead of ADWIN/HDDM-A on gradual; the Stage-1-only variants are the right tool there (S1_classical 3.0 abrupt, S1_both 1.0 gradual).

docs.title: Per dataset
docs.text:
Dataset DF-H ADWIN HDDM-A HDDM-W PageHinkley Covtype 7.9 8.8 11.7 6.1 10.4 Electricity 6.8 11.1 11.0 8.8 14.7

DF-H beats ADWIN, HDDM-A and PageHinkley on both datasets. HDDM-W wins Covtype (6.1 vs 7.9) but loses Electricity (8.8 vs 6.8); the overall rank is close (7.47 vs 7.34).

docs.title: Detection delay
docs.text: Mean mdt over all detected cells: DF-H 1,038, ADWIN 851, HDDM-W 939, HDDM-A 1,195, SEED 827, STEPD 846. The label-free Stage 1 is faster (S1_deep 861, S1_both 873) because it does not wait for confirmation. That is the trade-off: DF-H buys precision/FAR with confirmation time. The Delay Tax result in E21 is the reason that trade-off matters.

docs.title: 4. Verdict
docs.text:
Capability proven against the requested panel.

  • DF-H is the best detector outside the KDD top two on this pilot, with the lowest FAR of the high-F1 rows.
  • It owns feature permutation against ADWIN/HDDM-A/HDDM-W/PageHinkley.
  • It is not a universal winner: SEED/STEPD beat it overall, HDDM-W beats it on Covtype and on abrupt filtering, and the Stage-1-only variants beat it on filtering.
  • The honest framing for the final report: DF-H is a strong feature-drift detector with a controlled false-alarm rate; SEED/STEPD remain the overall default, and the unique contribution is the label-free warning under delay (E21).

Caveats. Two datasets, five trials, no significance testing; PageHinkley's F1 is near zero, so its low FAR is not a capability claim; the E18/E19 signal-gate negatives still stand. This is a focused capability check on the data in the repo, not a new benchmark.

What this page is: the progress report for everything built after the mid-term baseline. It is grounded in the git history and in the saved artifacts under experiments/results/, not in memory or in the commit messages.

docs.title: Bottom line
docs.text:
• The corrected comparison is 74.8 ± 61.8 vs 515.0 ± 97.1 samples·κ on the 5,000-sample window (≈6.9×, not 294×), and 321.4 vs 3,472.9 over the rest of the stream (≈10.8×). The frozen model recovered on 0/11 seeds; the streaming model had a real recovery on 8/11.
  • The legacy 294× and 24× figures are retired. The worst streaming seed is 0.74× the best frozen seed on the clean panel.
  • On synthetic data, HDDM-A on the raw mistake signal remains the best default for all four drift shapes. On real Elec2 it is host-conditional: it wins all four shapes on the static Hoeffding Tree, but ADWIN wins abrupt (1.000 vs 0.400) and recurring (0.770 vs 0.593) on the adaptive HAT.
  • The KDD'26 reproduction ranks SEED and STEPD first (2.12), HDDM-W third (3.56), HDDM-A fourth (3.87); the F1 values match the paper's tables.
  • The baseline ladder's 5-seed slice shows scheduled retraining cuts full-stream damage sharply but only marginally improves fixed-window damage, because its 12k refit buffer delays recovery. Adaptive streaming learners have lower damage and the only non-zero recovery rates.
  • The Delay Tax, the ABCD/ABCD(X) reproduction, the system chapter and the final report are not started or not finished. They are the plan in §8.
