docs.title: 3. What was built: the DriftLab harness
docs.text:
Before the mid-term, Exp-01 and Exp-02 were bespoke scripts with duplicated metric code. After it, one config-driven runner expresses every experiment.

Module Responsibility driftlab/config.py Typed experiment config, YAML loading, stable config_hash driftlab/streams.py SEA, Hyperplane, RandomRBF, Agrawal; Elec2 and Phishing; label-swap, feature-permutation, gradual/incremental/recurring episodes; per-seed shuffling driftlab/detectors.py ADWIN, KSWIN, Page-Hinkley, DDM, EDDM, FHDDM, HDDM-A, HDDM-W; raw and EWMA channels driftlab/learners.py Frozen RF, scheduled RF, oracle refit, River HT/HAT/ARF/Leveraging Bagging/ADWIN Bagging driftlab/metrics.py Accuracy, Cohen κ, rolling windows, damage_ref, damage_full, AUE, recovery, dip, calibration driftlab/deep/ DriftFormer (feature-token transformer, memory heads, replay, self-supervised loss, drift-triggered head reset), DeepRiver rolling, pretraining and training driftlab/harness.py Prequential loop, per-seed units, resume, artifact writing, acceptance verdicts driftlab/artifacts.py meta.json, summary.json, results.json, episodes.jsonl, detections.jsonl, series.npz, figures, cache driftlab/figures.py, stats.py, calibration.py Re-render figures from artifacts; Friedman/Nemenyi helpers; ECE/Brier experiments/run.py CLI: --exp, --seeds, --limit, --out, --resume, --device, --figure-only, --report experiments/registry/ 16 experiment configs (e01–e15, e17) experiments/{detector,schedule,delay,cost}_report.py Derived analyses with no new model runs

Artifact contract. A run is reproducible from meta.json (config, config hash, git SHA, versions, command) plus the committed artifact files. Figures are re-rendered from the artifact with --figure-only; they are never hand-drawn.

Engineering hardening added after the mid-term (working tree).

  • --resume with a config-hash guard: a changed config refuses to resume into an old artifact.
  • Per-seed cache units (s<stream>_seed<seed>), so an interrupted sweep restarts at the next unit instead of the beginning.
  • --device auto|cpu|cuda override for deep models, leaving River models alone.
  • Acceptance semantics fixed: an experiment with no acceptance rules reports pass = null ("nothing was asserted"), not a false pass.
  • series.npz export for downstream figures.
  • schedule_report.py rewritten to run the KS phase-noise test and to state when the refit buffer makes the uniformity test invalid.

Tests and CI. 53 test functions across 9 files (metrics, streams, detectors, artifacts, delay, acceptance, resume, device, KDD runner). The CI workflow added in ed2c144 runs uv sync, pytest experiments/tests -q, and a 1,500-sample smoke run of E02.

docs.title: 4.1 E01 — the damage metric was wrong; the claim survived
docs.text:
The defect. The legacy damage_area integrated from τ to the recovery point. On 8/11 seeds the recovery rule collapsed to τ (the model never left its band), so the streaming integral covered one sample while the frozen integral — which never recovered — covered the whole window. Both 294× and 24× were upper bounds of a truncated integral.

The fix. damage_ref integrates max(κ_ref − κ(t), 0) over a fixed 5,000-sample window with a panel-shared κ_ref; damage_full does the same over the rest of the stream; recovery only counts after a real band exit.

Metric (11 seeds) DeepRiver Frozen RF Timing oracle Full-run accuracy 0.8830 ± 0.0021 0.8539 ± 0.0017 0.8543 ± 0.0016 Full-run Cohen κ 0.7530 ± 0.0044 0.6850 ± 0.0035 0.6860 ± 0.0033 damage_ref (primary) 74.8 ± 61.8 515.0 ± 97.1 505.0 ± 97.6 damage_full 321.4 ± 203.8 3,472.9 ± 559.7 3,425.4 ± 506.8 AUE vs oracle −0.0472 ± 0.0058 +0.0010 ± 0.0027 0 recovery_rate 8/11 0/11 0/11 Recovery samples (recovered) 285–4,279 (mean 1,502) never never

Verdict. DeepRiver's damage_ref is lower on 11/11 seeds. Frozen recovered on 0/11. The corrected mean gap is ≈6.9×; the full-stream gap is ≈10.8×; the worst DeepRiver seed (217.9) is 0.74× the best frozen seed (295.2). The acceptance block passes: frozen never recovers, and the treatment wins the damage comparison on all 11 seeds.

Panel-composition note. The committed artifact at HEAD contains a five-model panel (DeepRiver, frozen, HT, HAT, oracle) from a host-default bug and reports 70.6 vs 504.4 (≈7.1×). The clean three-model rerun in the working tree archived that panel at experiments/results/_archive/e01_5model/ and reports 74.8 vs 515.0. Because damage_ref uses a panel-shared reference, removing the two misconfigured hosts moved every number; the clean panel is the authority.

docs.title: 4.2 E02 — the no-drift control: smoothing is not free
docs.text:
E02 ran two stationary streams × 5 seeds × every model and all eight detectors on raw and EWMA channels (220 detections). Nothing should ring.

Detector (static HT) Raw FAR /1k EWMA FAR /1k Worst-cell FAR Gate (≤0.1) ADWIN 0.008 0.522 0.548 FAIL KSWIN 0.000 7.667 7.667 FAIL PageHinkley 0.047 0.043 0.055 PASS

Verdict. The models stay stable on both stationary streams, so the control does its sanity job. But the overall FAR gate fails: smoothing the mistake signal makes ADWIN and KSWIN fire on a world that has not changed. The raw channel is the default; EWMA is a diagnostic. This is why the detector maps use raw as the headline channel.

docs.title: 4.3 E04 — the synthetic detector map
docs.text:
Design. Four generators (SEA, Hyperplane, RandomRBF, Agrawal) × four drift shapes × eight detectors × two hosts × raw/EWMA, five seeds. 240 model runs, 300 episodes, 1,760 detector runs, 4,867 s.

Drift shape Best default F1 Episode recall FAR /1k NDT Abrupt HDDM-A, raw 0.683 0.75 0.0075 0.185 Gradual HDDM-A, raw 0.842 0.95 0.0083 0.155 Incremental HDDM-A, raw 0.883 0.90 0.0033 0.012 Recurring HDDM-A, raw 0.500 0.725 0.0308 0.144

Verdict. HDDM-A on the raw signal is the best cell for all four synthetic shapes; recurring drift is the hard case. E04's acceptance block records pass = true; this remains a 5-seed first pass with default detector settings, not the full tuned matrix.

Bug found and fixed. The first report selected KSWIN for incremental with F1 = 1.0 and episode recall = 0.25 — impossible. Zero-alarm runs had precision = None and were dropped from the F1 mean, so a detector that never rang looked perfect. The corrected report recomputes F1 from raw TP/FP/episode counts and scores zero alarms as F1 = 0. The KSWIN "perfect" cell is retired.

docs.title: 4.4 E17 — the detector map on real Elec2
docs.text:
Design. 45,312 real electricity-market records, shuffled per seed, with a known label swap 0 → 1 injected at τ = 22,656. Four shapes, eight detectors, two hosts, raw/EWMA, five seeds. 60 model runs, 75 episodes, 440 detections, 832 s.

Drift shape HDDM-A, static HT ADWIN, static HT HDDM-A, adaptive HAT ADWIN, adaptive HAT Abrupt 0.933 0.452 0.400 1.000 Gradual 0.960 0.495 1.000 1.000 Incremental 0.960 0.842 1.000 0.971 Recurring 0.787 0.508 0.593 0.770

Best host/channel per detector (mean F1 over four shapes): ADWIN 0.935, HDDM-A 0.910, PageHinkley 0.788, FHDDM 0.715, HDDM-W 0.580, DDM 0.573, KSWIN 0.506, EDDM 0.413.

Verdict. The E04 default is host-conditional on real data. HDDM-A's one-sided test only alarms when the error rate rises significantly above its frozen low-error reference; HAT adapts and can repair an abrupt label swap before the test separates. ADWIN compares two windows two-sidedly and still sees the change. Recurring change remains the hard case. Caveats: one dataset, one injected mechanism, five seeds, shuffled rows remove natural temporal drift. E17 has no acceptance rules, so the artifact reports pass = null ("nothing was asserted"). Its report page also references figures while experiments/results/e17/figures/ is empty — this must be rendered before the site build is treated as final.

docs.title: 4.5 E03 — the baseline ladder and the phase-noise test
docs.text:
Design. SEA + Hyperplane, abrupt drift with the onset jittered by ±7,000 samples so each seed hits a different retrain phase. Ten models: frozen RF, scheduled RF every 1k/5k/20k (12k refit window), HT, HAT, ARF, Leveraging Bagging, ADWIN Bagging, oracle refit. The completed slice is 5 seeds × 2 streams × 10 models = 100 runs, 2,904 s. The full 11-seed run is 20/22 seed-stream units, 200/220 model runs and has not been summarized.

Model Accuracy Cohen κ damage_ref damage_full Recovery rate Dip Frozen RF 0.809 0.608 870.3 5,393.9 0.00 0.237 Scheduled RF (1k) 0.855 0.702 745.5 1,264.7 0.00 0.219 Scheduled RF (5k) 0.850 0.694 826.1 1,658.7 0.00 0.232 Scheduled RF (20k) 0.841 0.674 875.4 2,376.5 0.00 0.237 Hoeffding Tree 0.844 0.679 742.8 1,875.2 0.00 0.211 HAT 0.848 0.689 473.0 1,320.0 0.50 0.183 ARF 0.839 0.671 592.0 1,866.7 0.40 0.211 Leveraging Bagging 0.857 0.707 515.1 1,006.6 0.30 0.180 ADWIN Bagging 0.853 0.699 631.4 1,167.0 0.20 0.193 Oracle refit 0.809 0.606 874.3 5,461.1 0.00 0.241

What the slice says.

  • Frozen RF is the highest of the deployable baselines (damage_ref 870.3); the pre-drift oracle is marginally higher at 874.3, which is the weak-oracle problem below. HAT (473.0) and Leveraging Bagging (515.1) pay roughly half, and only the adaptive learners have non-zero recovery rates.
  • Frequent scheduled retraining cuts full-stream damage sharply (5,393.9 → 1,264.7, ≈4.3×) but barely moves the fixed-window damage (870.3 → 745.5, ≈1.17×). The 12k refit buffer is longer than the 1k interval, so the refit itself delays the recovery it is supposed to provide.
  • The oracle refit is not an upper bound: it is refit on pre-drift data, so its damage_ref (874.3) is essentially frozen. The same weakness appeared in E01's timing oracle. A real upper bound needs post-drift data or a stronger definition.

Phase-noise test. The pre-registered expectation was that scheduled recovery scatters uniformly over the retrain interval.

Scheduled model Mean recovery Uniform mean KS p Uniform not rejected? Valid test? 1k 6,575 500 0.000 no no — buffer 12k > interval 1k 5k 8,926 2,500 2.6e-28 no no — buffer 12k > interval 5k 20k 9,683 10,000 0.081 yes yes — interval 20k > buffer 12k

The 1k and 5k cells cannot test phase noise: the recovery lag is buffer-dominated, not phase-dominated. The only valid cell (20k) is consistent with uniform phase. The honest conclusion is not "phase noise is uniform"; it is "the test needs a refit buffer shorter than the retrain interval, and only the 20k cell currently satisfies that". E03 needs a design fix before the phase-noise claim is usable.

E03's acceptance block passes for the slice (ARF's AUE is better than scheduled 5k), but this is a 5-seed slice, not the full pre-registered matrix.

docs.text:
Design. Elec2 (45,312 rows) and Phishing (1,250 rows), each with label-swap and feature-permutation drift injected at a known position; five seeds; frozen RF, ARF, HAT, DriftFormer, oracle. 100 runs, 738 s, CUDA.

Model (20 cells) Accuracy Cohen κ damage_ref damage_full Recovery rate Frozen RF 0.685 0.395 297.4 4,703.0 0.00 ARF 0.875 0.724 198.0 2,684.8 0.20 HAT 0.803 0.583 245.7 3,019.6 0.15 DriftFormer 0.770 0.524 284.9 3,497.5 0.00 Oracle refit 0.698 0.415 280.3 4,518.3 0.00

By dataset.

Dataset Model damage_ref Cohen κ Recovery rate Elec2 ARF 202.4 0.666 0.00 Elec2 HAT 268.3 0.593 0.00 Elec2 Frozen RF 295.0 0.392 0.00 Elec2 DriftFormer 314.7 0.545 0.00 Phishing ARF 193.5 0.782 0.40 Phishing HAT 223.0 0.573 0.30 Phishing DriftFormer 255.2 0.503 0.00 Phishing Frozen RF 299.8 0.397 0.00

Verdict (provisional). ARF leads on both real datasets, with lower damage_ref and higher full-run κ than frozen. HAT is second. DriftFormer, the new deep model, does not beat ARF and on Elec2 pays slightly more damage than frozen (314.7 vs 295.0), although it beats frozen on κ (0.545 vs 0.392). Recovery rates are low everywhere; real-stream drift is harder than SEA. E14 has no acceptance rules (pass = null), only five seeds and two datasets, and Phishing has just 1,250 rows. Do not quote this as a field-wide result.

docs.title: 4.7 KDD'26 — the external detector benchmark reproduction
docs.text:
Design. Seven real datasets, four injected drift types, abrupt and gradual transitions, 50 Monte Carlo trials per cell, six detectors. 2,800 tasks, 0 failures, 16,800 result rows, 13m33s wall time on 14 workers.

Detector 10-trial rank 50-trial rank Mean F1 (56 cells) SEED 2.23 2.12 0.300 STEPD 2.30 2.12 0.303 HDDM-W 3.56 3.56 0.163 HDDM-A 3.94 3.87 0.155 DDM 4.52 4.54 0.101 ADWIN 4.45 4.80 0.122

Verdict. The 50-trial run confirms the 10-trial pilot: SEED and STEPD tie for first, and HDDM-A is fourth, behind HDDM-W. This directly contradicts the synthetic-only "HDDM-A is the default" reading and supports E17's host-conditional conclusion. The absolute F1 values reproduce the paper's tables for the shared detectors — abrupt feature permutation 0.572/0.526/0.313/0.237 here vs 0.61/0.53/0.36/0.25 published; gradual 0.424/0.442/0.089/0.122 vs 0.46/0.45/0.10/0.14; DDM's abrupt feature-permutation F1 0.021 vs 0.02.

Protocol discrepancy, resolved by measurement. The public benchmark code feeds correctness (int(true == pred)) into MOA detectors that document 1 = error, and its gradual window is (onset, onset) rather than the paper's end-anchored window. kdd_bench.py implements both conventions. The headline uses --signal correct --gradual-anchor code because that reproduces the published F1 tables; the paper-protocol defaults give the same top two and the same mid-tier HDDM-A rank (3.91). The ranking is robust to the convention.

Not reproduced. The ABCD/ABCD(X) arm is the expensive part of the matrix, overheats the 16-thread laptop CPU, and is not needed for the HDDM-A conclusion. It is cited, not reproduced: the paper's ABCD(X) average rank is 1.0 abrupt and 3.3 gradual. This should be stated as a limitation, not hidden.

docs.title: 6.2 What the evidence supports
docs.text:
• A frozen model never recovered after the SEA drift (0/11 seeds).
  • A streaming model's corrected damage is ≈6.9× lower in the fixed window and ≈10.8× lower over the rest of the stream; it wins on 11/11 seeds.
  • HDDM-A raw is the best default on the synthetic static host, but not universally: on real Elec2's adaptive HAT, ADWIN wins abrupt and recurring.
  • The KDD'26 ranking reproduces: SEED/STEPD first, HDDM-A mid-tier.
  • Scheduled retraining helps the full stream (≈4.3× at 1k) but only marginally helps the fixed drift window (≈1.17×), because its refit buffer delays recovery.
  • On the two real streams tested, ARF beats frozen on damage and κ.

docs.title: 6.3 What the evidence does not support
docs.text:
• 294× or 24× as the size of the effect. They are retired upper bounds.
  • "HDDM-A is the best detector" without a host qualifier.
  • "Streaming always wins on real data": DriftFormer loses to frozen on Elec2 damage and never recovers; only ARF/HAT show the advantage.
  • "Recovery time is a single number": it is 285–4,279 on recovered seeds and undefined on the rest.
  • Any Delay Tax claim: zero experiments have run.
  • Any ABCD/ABCD(X) claim from this repo: that row is cited, not reproduced.
  • Any statistical significance across datasets: E14 has two datasets and five seeds; Friedman/Nemenyi has not been run.

docs.title: Results — the measured verdicts, all experiments
docs.text:
What this page is: the project's global results file. One page that holds the conclusion of every experiment — not the effort, not the logs, not the milestones: the bottom line, the numbers that back it, and the process that produced it. Written for management review; every figure and number traces to a data artifact (experiments/*/results.json).

How this page updates: an experiment is added here only when it concludes, as a single row in the verdict registry (§4) plus its measured evidence (§3). The global verdict (§1) is re-stated over all concluded experiments whenever one lands.

Status 12 concluded: Exp-01, Exp-02, E01 metric v2 correction (clean panel), E03 baseline ladder (11 seeds), E04 detector map first pass (5 seeds), E14 real-stream model check (provisional 5-seed slice), E17 real-stream detector check (5 seeds), KDD'26 six-detector reproduction (50 trials), E18 deep-signal gate (negative), E19 DF-H v1 pilot (gate failed), E21 Delay Tax fixed-delay headline, E22 detector shootout (DF-H beats the requested classical panel); E21 is the surviving headline (Roadmap v2) Data artifacts experiments/exp01/results.json · experiments/exp02/results.json · experiments/results/e01/ (corrected metric, clean rerun) · experiments/results/e03/ (baseline ladder) · experiments/results/e04/ (detector map) · experiments/results/e14/ (real-stream model check) · experiments/results/e17/ (real-stream detector check) · experiments/results/e18/ + experiments/data/deep_signals/pilot/ (deep signal gate) · experiments/results/e19_kdd_pilot/ (DF-H v1 pilot) · experiments/results/e21/ (Delay Tax fixed-delay headline) · experiments/results/e22_detector_shootout/ (detector shootout) · experiments/results/kdd_bench_full/ (KDD'26 reproduction) · experiments/results/_archive/e01_5model/ (pre-fix panel, superseded) Method / protocol thesis.md · streaming-vs-batch-metrics.md Formatting note unicode math (τ, κ₀, Δκ, ≈, ≥) renders identically in Obsidian, GitHub, mkdocs

docs.title: 1. The global verdict
docs.text:
A model that keeps learning from the stream heals itself after a concept change — a model that was trained once and frozen does not. Across 11 seeds: the frozen model recovered on 0 of 11 runs. The corrected metric (E01) prices the damage over a fixed 5,000-sample window with a panel-shared reference: 74.8 ± 61.8 vs 515.0 ± 97.1 samples·κ, a ≈ 6.9× gap. Over the rest of the stream the gap is ≈ 10.8× (321.4 vs 3,472.9). The streaming model also wins the overall averages: 88.3% vs 85.4% accuracy, 0.753 vs 0.685 Cohen Kappa. Recovery is 8/11 seeds with a real excursion (285–4,279 samples); the old “0 on 8/11” was an artefact of the τ-anchored rule. The legacy 294× and 24× figures are retired as upper bounds; on the clean panel the worst DeepRiver seed (217.9) is 0.74× the best frozen seed (295.2).

Detector track (2026-11-14). E18/E19 are negative on their pre-registered gates, but the focused E22 shootout shows DF-H is 3rd overall (7.34), ahead of HDDM-W (7.47), ADWIN (9.94), HDDM-A (11.34) and PageHinkley (12.53) — behind only the KDD top two, SEED and STEPD — with a 0.04 FAR and a clear feature-permutation win. E21 is the surviving headline: a label-free Stage-1 warning in 70–513 samples vs 2,120–3,269 for the error-only panel at L = 2,000. The detector is a strong feature-drift warning system, not a top-2 universal detector.

Metric correction — read this before quoting any number below

Sections 3a and 3b use the original damage_area definition, which integrated from τ to the recovery point. On 8/11 seeds recovery collapsed to τ, truncating the streaming integral. 294× and 24× are upper bounds and are retired. The corrected numbers are in §3c and E01-metric-v2.md.

Figure 1 — how every experiment in this file runs: one stream, two models in the same race, one prequential scoreboard, one verdict. No result below was produced any other way.

docs.title: Why this matters, in one line each
docs.text: Streaming model (keeps learning) Frozen model (trained once) Reacts to change on its own? Yes — adapts on its own error signal No — waits for a human to retrain Recovery after the drift at τ 8/11 seeds with a real excursion; 285–4,279 samples never — 0 of 11 seeds recovered Skill lost, corrected damage_ref (5k window) 74.8 ± 61.8 samples·κ (worst 217.9) 515.0 ± 97.1 samples·κ (best 295.2) Skill lost over the rest of the stream (damage_full) 321.4 ± 203.8 samples·κ 3,472.9 ± 559.7 samples·κ Overall quality (full run, 48k samples) 0.883 acc · 0.753 κ 0.854 acc · 0.685 κ

docs.title: 2. The process — how results are produced
docs.text:
One experiment = one controlled race, run identically for both models on the same data in the same order. Three non-negotiable rules keep the comparison fair:

  1. Prequential scoring — every sample is scored before it trains the model (test-then-train). No model ever sees a future sample.
  2. Same warm-up, same data — both models train on the same first 20% of the stream; the frozen model never updates after that, the streaming model updates on every sample.
  3. Measured, not asserted — every number in this file is read from a committed results.json; figures are re-rendered from that file, never hand-drawn.

The scoreboard metrics used in every verdict:

Metric What it measures Good direction Accuracy / Cohen Kappa (rolling, w = 1,000) classification skill over time, chance-corrected ↑ κ_ref — shared pre-drift reference mean pre-drift skill across the model panel reference level Δκ — dip depth how much skill the drift knocks off, relative to κ_ref ↓ (shallower) recovery_rate fraction of episodes with a real band exit followed by 500 in-band samples ↑ damage_ref (primary) fixed-window integral Σ max(κ_ref − κ(t), 0) — cannot be gamed by a weak model's own baseline ↓ damage_full the same integral over the rest of the stream ↓ AUE mean error minus the timing-oracle error; secondary, because the oracle is not an upper bound ↓ ~~Recovery time / damage area~~ legacy Exp-01/02 definitions; kept only for audit, superseded by E01 —

docs.title: 3a. Exp-01 — SEA, one abrupt drift (seed 42)
docs.text:
The first data point. Measured 2026-09-09, seed 42, 60,000 samples, abrupt drift at τ = 30,000, 10% label noise. Streaming model: DeepRiver rolling deep classifier (RNN head, window = 500). Frozen model: Random Forest (100 trees) trained once on the warm-up. Full series: experiments/exp01/results.json.

Figure 2 — the overall race, 48,000 post-warm-up samples. The streaming model wins the cumulative scoreboard as well as the reactivity contest: +2.9 pp accuracy and +6.8 pp Cohen Kappa.

Figure 3 — the verdict in one picture. Before the drift both models sit at the same skill level (κ₀ ≈ 0.755–0.759). At τ the frozen model (red) falls to 0.592 and stays down; the streaming model (blue) dips only to 0.703 and is back inside its own band 835 samples later — with no human intervention.

Figure 4 — the two decisive columns. Recovery: 835 samples vs never. Damage paid for the drift: 31 vs 3,307 samples·κ (log scale).

Drift-window metric (τ = 30,000) Streaming (DeepRiver rolling) Frozen (RF) Pre-drift baseline κ₀ 0.755 0.759 Minimum rolling Kappa after τ 0.703 0.592 Dip depth Δκ 0.052 (shallow) 0.167 (3× deeper) Recovery time 835 samples — inside the pre-registered 5,000 budget never Damage area 31 samples·κ 3,307 samples·κ

docs.title: 3b. Exp-02 — the 11-seed sweep (is Exp-01's number reproducible?)
docs.text:
The statistical data point. Measured 2026-09-12: exactly the Exp-01 replica — same stream, same two models, same warm-up, same prequential loop, same metric definitions — rerun on 11 seeds (42, Exp-01's, plus 0–9), changing nothing but the seed. Full per-seed detail: experiments/exp02/results.json. Seed 42 reproduced Exp-01 exactly (835 samples, delta 0), so the sweep is a genuine rerun of the same experiment.

Figure 5 — left: recovery time per seed; 8 of 11 seeds sit on the metric floor (0 = never left the pre-drift band) and the rest recover in 174–2,497 samples, all inside the 5,000 budget. Right: damage area per seed (log scale); the 5 seeds with exactly zero measured damage are drawn as hatched stubs. The damage gap is stable; the recovery number is not.

Metric (11 seeds) Streaming (DeepRiver rolling) Frozen (RF) Pre-drift baseline κ₀ 0.751 ± 0.017 0.767 ± 0.018 Dip depth Δκ 0.045 ± 0.015 0.173 ± 0.018 Recovery time (samples from τ) median 0, mean 319 ± 765 (0 / 174 / 835 / 2,497) never, 11/11 Damage area (samples·κ) 13 ± 31 (median ≈ 0.001, max 103) 3,710 ± 592 (min 2,439, max 4,368) Full-run accuracy 0.8830 ± 0.0021 0.8539 ± 0.0017 Full-run Cohen Kappa 0.7530 ± 0.0044 0.6850 ± 0.0035

Figure 6 — the same damage numbers as a distribution: one dot per seed, median marked. Every frozen seed sits in a narrow band; every streaming seed is two orders of magnitude below it. Median ≈ 0.001 vs 3,822 samples·κ.

What the sweep settles. Exp-01's specific 835 was a property of seed 42, not of the method: across 11 seeds the recovery time is 0 on eight seeds (no excursion to recover from) and 174 / 835 / 2,497 on the other three. What is stable is everything the claim actually rests on — the frozen model never recovers (0/11, no exceptions), the damage gap is two orders of magnitude on the mean and 24× even worst-case-vs-best-case, and the streaming dip is consistently ~3.8× shallower. Exp-02 also mildly restores Exp-01's refuted control expectation: the frozen model does start ahead while the concept is stationary (κ₀ 0.767 vs 0.751), and still loses the full run because it collapses at τ.

One methodological finding, recorded not patched. The recovery-time rule looks for the first sustained in-band run starting at τ, so a model that stays in band for the first 500 samples and dips afterwards is scored 0. Seven of eleven seeds did leave the band after τ, but only the three with an early excursion are credited with a recovery time — which makes recovery non-monotone in dip depth (seed 3 dips deeper than seed 9 yet scores 0). Damage area and dip depth are the trustworthy drift-window metrics; recovery time is meaningful only conditional on an early excursion. Details in the Exp-02 write-up §6c.

Figure 7 — the flaw in one picture. Green = an excursion early enough for its recovery to be credited; orange X = a seed that did leave its band but was scored 0 because the excursion began after τ + 500; hollow blue = never left the band. Four of the eleven seeds are orange — which is why the mean recovery time is not a property of the model.

docs.title: 3c. E01 — corrected metric v2 (11 seeds, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
This supersedes the damage numbers in 3a and 3b. E01 re-ran the same SEA/DeepRiver vs frozen pilot with a fixed-window, panel-shared damage metric and recovery conditional on a real band exit.

Metric (11 seeds) DeepRiver Frozen RF damage_ref (5k window, primary) 74.8 ± 61.8 (worst 217.9) 515.0 ± 97.1 (best 295.2) damage_full (rest of stream) 321.4 ± 203.8 3,472.9 ± 559.7 AUE vs timing oracle −0.0472 ± 0.0058 +0.0010 ± 0.0027 recovery_rate 8/11 0/11 Recovery time, recovered seeds 285–4,279 (mean 1,502) never Full-run accuracy / Cohen κ 0.883 / 0.753 0.854 / 0.685

Figure 8 — the corrected comparison. Left: damage_ref; right: AUE against the timing oracle. AUE is secondary because the timing oracle knows when the drift happened but not what the new concept is; its own damage (505) is almost identical to frozen. The primary result is the damage_ref gap.

Verdict. Frozen recovered on 0/11 seeds. DeepRiver's damage_ref was lower on 11/11 seeds, with a ≈6.9× mean gap and a ≈10.8× full-stream gap. On the clean panel the worst DeepRiver seed (217.9) is 0.74× the best frozen seed (295.2), so the legacy 24× worst-case claim is retired along with the 294× mean. The clean headline is: the frozen model never recovers, and the streaming model pays roughly one seventh of the fixed-window damage. The full write-up is E01-metric-v2.md.

Clean panel

The E01 rerun contains only DeepRiver, frozen RF, and the timing oracle. The earlier artifact that also included HT/HAT (a since-fixed host-default bug) is archived at experiments/results/_archive/e01_5model/ and is superseded by the numbers above.

docs.title: 3d. E04 — detector map, first pass (5 seeds, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
Eight detectors were replayed on the raw and smoothed mistake streams of two hosts, across four generators and four drift shapes. This is the first map of “which alarm works for which change”.

Drift shape Best default Balanced score Changes caught False alarms /1k Detection delay Abrupt HDDM-A, raw 0.683 75% 0.0075 0.185 Gradual HDDM-A, raw 0.842 95% 0.0083 0.155 Incremental HDDM-A, raw 0.883 90% 0.0033 0.012 Recurring HDDM-A, raw 0.500 73% 0.0308 0.144

Figure 9 — balanced score per detector and drift shape on the static host, raw signal. HDDM-A is the best cell for every shape; recurring drift is the hard case.

Verdict. HDDM-A on the raw signal is the sensible default across all four shapes. Recurring change is the hard case (0.50); incremental is the easiest (0.88). Smoothing the mistake signal raises false alarms without improving the ranking; the raw channel is the default and the smoothed channel is a diagnostic. This is a 5-seed first pass with default detector settings, not the full pre-registered matrix. The full write-up is E04-detector-map.md.

Scoring bug found and fixed

The first E04 report selected KSWIN for incremental with F1 = 1.0 and episode recall = 0.25. That was impossible: zero-alarm runs had precision = None and were excluded from the F1 mean. The corrected report recomputes F1 from raw TP/FP/episode counts and treats zero alarms as F1 = 0. The “KSWIN perfect” result is retired.

docs.title: 3e. E17 — the detector map on a real stream (Elec2, 5 seeds, 2026-11-13)
docs.text:
E04's eight detectors were replayed on real electricity-market records: 45,312 rows of Elec2, shuffled per seed, with a known label-swap drift injected at τ = 22,656. This is the first real-data check of the detector map. Mean over 5 seeds, raw channel, corrected balanced score:

Drift shape HDDM-A, static HT ADWIN, static HT HDDM-A, adaptive HAT ADWIN, adaptive HAT Abrupt 0.933 0.452 0.400 1.000 Gradual 0.960 0.495 1.000 1.000 Incremental 0.960 0.842 1.000 0.971 Recurring 0.787 0.508 0.593 0.770

Verdict. The E04 default is host-conditional on real data. On the static Hoeffding Tree, HDDM-A repeats the synthetic result and wins all four shapes. On the adaptive HAT it does not: ADWIN wins abrupt (1.000 vs 0.400) and recurring (0.770 vs 0.593), ties gradual, and loses only incremental. Across the better host/channel per detector, mean F1 is ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910. The one-sided Hoeffding test can miss an abrupt change that an adaptive learner repairs quickly; ADWIN's two-sided window comparison still sees it. Recurring remains the hard case. Five seeds, one dataset, one injected mechanism — this is a warning, not a final ranking. The full write-up is E17-real-detector-map.md.

docs.title: 3f. E14 — the real-stream model check (5 seeds, 2026-11-14)
docs.text:
E14 replayed the streaming-vs-frozen comparison on real features and labels: Elec2 (45,312 rows) and Phishing (1,250 rows), with label-swap and feature-permutation drift injected at a known point. Five seeds, 100 runs, metric v2. Pooled over 20 dataset × mechanism × seed cells:

Model Accuracy Cohen κ damage_ref damage_full Recovery rate Frozen RF 0.685 0.395 297.4 4,703.0 0.00 ARF 0.875 0.724 198.0 2,684.8 0.20 HAT 0.803 0.583 245.7 3,019.6 0.15 DriftFormer 0.770 0.524 284.9 3,497.5 0.00 Oracle refit 0.698 0.415 280.3 4,518.3 0.00

Verdict. ARF leads on both datasets (Elec2 damage_ref 202.4 vs frozen 295.0; Phishing 193.5 vs 299.8), and the provisional acceptance rules pass: pooled damage ratio 0.666×, ARF lower in 18/20 cells, frozen recovered 0/20, κ gain +0.329. DriftFormer beats frozen on κ but not on damage — on Elec2 it pays slightly more (314.7 vs 295.0). That is the expected negative that justifies using the deep model as a signal extractor, not as the KDD host. Two datasets, five seeds and one injected mechanism per stream: provisional, not field-wide. The full write-up is E14-real-streams.md.

docs.title: 3g. E03 — the baseline ladder (11 seeds, 2026-11-14)
docs.text:
E03 ran the full 11-seed ladder on SEA and Hyperplane: frozen RF, three scheduled-retrain intervals, static and adaptive trees, ARF, Leveraging Bagging, ADWIN Bagging, and the timing oracle. 220 model runs, 220 episodes.

Model Accuracy Cohen κ AUE damage_ref Recovery rate Leveraging Bagging 0.857 0.707 −0.0469 455.7 1.000 HAT 0.847 0.685 −0.0447 489.2 0.955 ARF 0.839 0.671 −0.0368 575.4 0.591 ADWIN Bagging 0.853 0.698 −0.0293 614.1 1.000 Hoeffding Tree 0.844 0.679 −0.0200 700.8 0.955 Scheduled RF, 1k 0.855 0.702 −0.0161 733.5 1.000 Scheduled RF, 5k 0.850 0.692 −0.0056 824.1 1.000 Scheduled RF, 20k 0.838 0.667 −0.0021 849.4 0.682 Frozen RF 0.810 0.609 +0.0004 871.7 0.000 Oracle refit 0.811 0.609 0.0000 864.3 0.000

Verdict. Every streaming adapter pays less damage than frozen RF and than every scheduled-retrain interval. The best streaming adapter is Leveraging Bagging (455.7), then HAT (489.2) and ARF (575.4); the 1k scheduled model is the best batch baseline (733.5) but still pays 1.6× the LB damage. The pre-registered acceptance cell passes: ARF's AUE (−0.0368) is better than scheduled-5k's (−0.0056).

Phase-noise caveat. The scheduled models recover by construction at each retrain tick, so recovery rate is not the comparison — damage_ref is. The phase-noise test is inconclusive: the refit buffer (12,000) is longer than the 1k and 5k intervals, so recovery lag is buffer-dominated, not phase-driven; only the 20k cell satisfies the design and it has one observation. The honest conclusion is that the ladder orders the models, not that recovery is uniform over a retrain interval. Artifact: experiments/results/e03/summary.json and schedule_test.json.

docs.title: 3h. E18 — the deep signal gate (80 cells, 2026-11-14)
docs.text:
A frozen SSL-pretrained DriftFormer encoder was asked whether its label-free signals beat the raw error rate on 2 datasets × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials. The pre-registered AUC gate was one deep signal at ≥ 0.75 and ≥ 0.10 above the error rate.

Signal AUC vs error feature_ks (classical control) 0.628 +0.029 embedding_shift 0.616 +0.017 embedding_var_shift 0.599 +0.000 error_rate 0.598 — ssl_loss 0.532 −0.067

Verdict: FAIL. Best deep signal 0.616, far short of 0.75. The deep view has power on feature permutation (embedding_var_shift 0.781), but the error rate is stronger there (0.879); label-only drift stays with Stage 2. A FAR-calibrated timing diagnostic at 0.1/1k shows Stage 1 detects feature permutation 2–5× earlier than error and detects feature filtering when error is blind — but the classical feature_ks control is often just as fast, so the deep marginal value is unproven. Full page: E18-deep-signals.md.

E18 — the deep signals cluster around the error-rate baseline overall; the feature-permutation cell is where they have real power, but the error rate is stronger there.

E18 timing — feature signals alarm before the error rate on feature permutation, and detect feature filtering where the error rate misses. “miss” means no alarm inside the 2,500-sample budget; percentages mark hit rates below 100%.

docs.title: 3i. E19 — DF-H v1 pilot (80 cells, 2026-11-14)
docs.text:
Rule-based fusion of Stage 1 (deep, classical, both) with SEED, STEPD, ADWIN and HDDM-A on the same 80 cells.

Detector Mean F1 FAR/1k Overall rank STEPD 0.281 0.05 5.22 SEED 0.267 0.06 5.44 DFH = 2of3_both 0.223 0.04 7.09 2of3_deep 0.221 0.04 7.12 HDDM-W 0.170 0.28 7.31 OR_deep 0.178 0.15 7.72 S1_both 0.160 0.13 8.50 AND_deep 0.201 0.01 8.53 ADWIN 0.117 0.11 9.59 2of3_nodeep (control) 0.154 0.03 9.97

Verdict: FAIL. DFH is 3rd, not top-2; it wins no feature cell as the primary, is tied 5th–7th on Covtype (average position 6.0; rank value 7.44), and passes only the FAR check (0.04 vs ADWIN 0.11). Ablations own feature cells (AND_deep abrupt permutation 1.50; S1_both gradual filtering 1.00), and DFH beats the no-feature control by 2.9 ranks — so the feature monitor adds information, but the fixed 2-of-3 rule is not top-2. No full E20 run; E21 Delay Tax is the next headline. Full page: E19-hybrid-detector.md.

E19 — DFH is third overall, behind STEPD and SEED, with the lowest FAR of the competitive rows.

E19 — the ablations own feature cells, but DFH is tied 5th–7th on Covtype and tied 3rd–4th on Electricity, so the strict dataset-robustness bar fails.

docs.title: 3j. E21 — the Delay Tax, fixed-delay headline (2026-11-14)
docs.text:
The surviving contribution. An error-only detector cannot react until the post-drift labels arrive, so its detection time is floor-bound at τ + L. A label-free Stage 1 monitor is not. This is the fixed-delay Lemma-1 synthesis on the same 80 KDD cells as E19.

At L = 2,000 samples, detection delay after onset:

Cell Stage 1 deep Stage 1 classical SEED STEPD ADWIN Covtype, abrupt 70 90 2,130 2,120 2,472 Covtype, gradual 306 406 2,710 2,616 — Electricity, abrupt 76 196 2,129 2,180 3,269 Electricity, gradual 293 513 2,701 2,694 —

Verdict: the label tax is real, and Stage 1 does not pay it. Stage 1 warns 4–30× earlier than the error-only panel at L = 2,000; its delay is flat in L, while every error-only detector shifts by L. The honest limit: Stage 1 is blind to label-only drift, so the result is a warning/confirmation split (T_warn vs T_confirm), not a standalone detector. The full stochastic/partial/selective/batch regime matrix is scaffolded but not yet run. Full page: E21-delay-detector.md.

E21 fixed-delay headline. Flat blue/gray lines are label-free Stage 1; dashed red/orange/purple lines are error-only detectors at base + L.

docs.title: 3k. E22 — detector shootout (80 cells, 2026-11-14)
docs.text:
A focused capability check on the datasets in the repo: our DF-H and Stage-1 monitor against ADWIN, HDDM-A, HDDM-W and PageHinkley, with SEED/STEPD as the KDD reference.

Detector Mean F1 FAR/1k Overall rank STEPD (ref) 0.281 0.05 5.44 SEED (ref) 0.267 0.06 5.59 DF-H (ours) 0.223 0.04 7.34 HDDM-W 0.170 0.28 7.47 Stage 1 both 0.160 0.13 8.66 Stage 1 deep 0.144 0.12 9.00 ADWIN 0.117 0.11 9.94 HDDM-A 0.128 0.04 11.34 PageHinkley 0.018 0.01 12.53

Verdict: DF-H beats the requested classical panel. It is 3rd overall, ahead of HDDM-W (7.47), ADWIN (9.94), HDDM-A (11.34) and PageHinkley (12.53), with the lowest FAR of the high-F1 rows. On feature permutation it beats every requested classical detector (5.8 abrupt / 5.5 gradual vs 8.8–16.0). It does not beat SEED/STEPD, HDDM-W wins Covtype (6.1 vs 7.9) and abrupt filtering (4.0 vs 11.5), and the Stage-1-only variants are the right tool on filtering. Full page: E22-detector-shootout.md.

E22 — DF-H is third overall and sits at low FAR; SEED/STEPD remain ahead. HDDM-W buys F1 with a much higher false-alarm rate; PageHinkley barely alarms and barely scores.

docs.title: 4. Verdict registry — one conclusion per experiment
docs.text:
The cumulative table. Rows land here only with a measured verdict; scheduled experiments are listed so the roadmap is visible, with their acceptance bar.

Exp Question asked Setting Verdict (measured) Conclusion Exp-01 ✅ (legacy metric) Can a streaming deep learner beat a frozen batch model on a drifting stream? SEA, one abrupt drift, 2 models, seed 42 Streaming wins — recovers in 835 samples (frozen: never); legacy damage 31 vs 3,307 Weakest form of the claim confirmed. The 835/damage numbers are superseded by E01 Exp-02 ✅ (legacy metric) Is the 835-sample recovery a fluke of one seed? SEA, one abrupt drift, 2 models, 11 seeds Streaming wins on every seed — frozen recovered 0/11; legacy damage 13 ± 31 vs 3,710 ± 592 (≈294×; 24× worst-vs-best) The claim generalises; the legacy magnitudes are upper bounds and retired by E01. Frozen still wins the stationary phase (κ₀ 0.767 vs 0.751) E01 ✅ Does the corrected metric preserve the Exp-01/02 verdict? SEA abrupt, 11 seeds, metric v2, clean panel Frozen recovered 0/11; DeepRiver damage_ref lower 11/11; 74.8 ± 61.8 vs 515.0 ± 97.1 (≈6.9×); damage_full 321.4 vs 3,472.9 (≈10.8×); recovery 8/11; worst-vs-best 0.74× The claim survives, the magnitude shrinks. 294× and 24× retired. AUE is secondary: the timing oracle is weak (damage 505). Panel is DeepRiver + frozen + oracle; the pre-fix four-model artifact is archived E04 ✅ (first pass, 5 seeds) Which detector works for which drift shape, and does the host matter? 4 generators × 4 shapes × 8 detectors × 2 hosts × raw/EWMA, 5 seeds HDDM-A raw is best for all four shapes; balanced score 0.683 abrupt, 0.842 gradual, 0.883 incremental, 0.500 recurring; recurring is hardest; EWMA raises false alarms One sensible default exists on the static host and synthetic generators; recurring drift is the hard case. A scoring bug that made a never-ringing detector look perfect was found and fixed. E17 shows the default is host-conditional on real Elec2; the full 11-seed matrix and tuning are pending E17 ✅ (real stream, 5 seeds) Does the E04 detector default survive on real data? Elec2 label-swap, 4 shapes × 8 detectors × 2 hosts × raw/EWMA, 5 seeds On static HT, HDDM-A raw wins all four (F1 0.933/0.960/0.960/0.787); on adaptive HAT, ADWIN wins abrupt (1.000 vs 0.400) and recurring (0.770 vs 0.593); best-host mean F1 ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910 The synthetic default is host-conditional; “wins all four” does not transfer to the adaptive host. Recurring remains hardest. The 50-trial KDD'26 run confirms SEED/STEPD (2.12) beat HDDM-A (3.87); ABCD/ABCD(X) is cited from the paper, not re-run KDD'26 ✅ (reproduction, 50 trials) Does HDDM-A remain the best detector on the paper's real-data benchmark? 7 real datasets × 4 drift types × abrupt/gradual × 6 detectors, 50 trials SEED and STEPD tie for first (avg rank 2.12; mean F1 0.300/0.303); HDDM-A is fourth (3.87; 0.155), behind HDDM-W (3.56); DDM 4.54; ADWIN 4.80 HDDM-A is not the best detector on real data. The ranking reproduces the KDD'26 paper and the F1 values match its tables. ABCD/ABCD(X) is cited from the paper, not re-run E03 ✅ (11 seeds) Does streaming also beat a scheduled-retrain batch model (the honest industrial baseline)? SEA + Hyperplane, 10-model ladder, 11 seeds, 220 runs Every streaming adapter beats frozen and every scheduled interval on damage_ref: LB 455.7, HAT 489.2, ARF 575.4 vs scheduled-1k 733.5 and frozen 871.7; acceptance AUE passes (ARF −0.0368 vs scheduled-5k −0.0056) The ladder confirms the damage ordering at 11 seeds. Phase-noise claim is inconclusive: the 12k refit buffer dominates the 1k/5k intervals; only the 20k cell is valid (n=1) E14 ✅ (provisional, 2 datasets × 5 seeds) Does the streaming win survive on real streams, and can DriftFormer host? Elec2 + Phishing, label-swap + feature-permutation, 5 seeds, 100 runs ARF leads both datasets: damage_ref 198.0 vs frozen 297.4 (0.666×), lower in 18/20 cells, κ 0.724 vs 0.395; frozen recovered 0/20; DriftFormer κ 0.524 and does not beat ARF Streaming adaptation survives the first real-stream check; DriftFormer is a signal extractor, not the host. Provisional: 2 datasets, 5 seeds; expansion deferred E18 ❌ (signal gate, 80 cells) Does a label-free deep signal beat the error rate? Covtype + Electricity × 4 drift types × 2 transitions × 5 trials Best deep AUC 0.616 vs error 0.598; feature permutation 0.781 vs 0.879; label-only ~0.51; timing at 0.1/1k: feature permutation 72–414 vs error 184–1,033; feature filtering detected where error is blind; feature_ks competitive Gate FAIL. Deep is a warning channel, not standalone; classical control travels to E19 E19 ❌ (DF-H v1 pilot, 80 cells) Does DF-H fusion beat the scalar panel? Same 80 cells; Stage 1 deep/classical/both + SEED/STEPD/ADWIN/HDDM-A DFH 3rd (rank 7.09; F1 0.223; FAR 0.04) behind STEPD 5.22 and SEED 5.44; no primary feature-cell win; Covtype tied 5th–7th; ablations AND_deep 1.50 abrupt permutation and S1_both 1.00 gradual filtering; beats no-feature control 9.97 Gate FAIL. Feature monitor adds value but not top-2; no full E20; E21 is next E21 ✅ (fixed-delay headline) Does label delay create a floor for error-only detectors that a label-free warning avoids? Same 80 KDD cells; Stage 1 vs SEED/STEPD/ADWIN at L = 0…10k At L = 2k: Stage 1 deep 70–513 samples vs SEED/STEPD 2,120–2,710 and ADWIN 2,472–3,269; Stage 1 flat in L, error-only shifts by L The surviving headline. Label-free warning is not floor-bound; the honest result is T_warn vs T_confirm, not a standalone detector. Full regime matrix scaffolded, not run E22 ✅ (detector shootout) What is DF-H capable of against ADWIN / HDDM-A / HDDM-W / PageHinkley? Same 80 cells; requested classical panel + SEED/STEPD reference DFH 3rd (7.34; F1 0.223; FAR 0.04) ahead of HDDM-W 7.47, ADWIN 9.94, HDDM-A 11.34, PageHinkley 12.53; behind STEPD 5.44/SEED 5.59; feature permutation 5.8/5.5 vs panel 8.8–16.0; Covtype HDDM-W 6.1 vs DFH 7.9 Capability proven vs the requested panel, not top-2; feature filtering better in the Stage-1-only ablation E15 ⏳ (replaced by E21) The Delay Tax: do delayed/rare labels starve batch retraining while streaming keeps working? label-delay sweep pending — replaced by E21 acceptance: streaming quality degrades slower under delay; E21 adds the DF-H detector benchmark

Scope guard: Exp-01 is deliberately the easiest possible version of the claim (one synthetic stream, no scheduled retrain, no label delay, single seed). Each row above removes one of those cushions. The global verdict stands on what is measured today and is re-stated as rows conclude.

docs.title: 5. The verdict vs what was promised
docs.text: The project pre-registered its expectations before running (thesis §6), so the results can be checked against the promises rather than reported after the fact.

docs.title: 5a. Exp-01 — pre-registered expectations vs measured
docs.text:
Pre-registered expectation Expected Measured (Exp-01) Verdict Streaming recovery is bounded ~250–350 samples 835 samples PASS (same order; well inside the 5,000-sample falsification budget) Frozen model never recovers never never (still depressed at stream end) PASS Frozen pays unbounded damage unbounded 3,307 vs 31 samples·κ PASS (≈ 106×) Dip is shallow for streaming, deep for frozen shallow vs deep 0.052 vs 0.167 PASS Frozen wins cumulative accuracy (honest control) batch ahead in steady state streaming wins 0.757 vs 0.689 REFUTED — in our favour on this seed

Figure 8 — pre-registered expectations (hatched) against measured results (blue): the measured recovery is inside the promised regime, and the measured damage gap is even larger than the thesis sketched.

docs.title: 5b. Exp-02 — pre-registered acceptance vs measured (legacy metric)
docs.text:
Pre-registered condition (fixed before the run) Required Measured Verdict Seeds ≥ 10 11 PASS Recovery reported as a distribution mean ± SD mean 319 ± 765, median 0, range 0–2,497 PASS — with a heavy-tail caveat: 8/11 seeds sit on the metric floor, so the mean is not a robust centre Streaming recovers on every seed every seed 11/11 (8 of them never left the band) PASS Frozen never recovers on every seed every seed 11/11 PASS H2: frozen wins steady state (restated control) frozen κ₀ ≥ streaming κ₀ frozen 0.767 vs streaming 0.751 SUPPORTED — unlike the single-seed Exp-01, where the two were level

Bottom line: the falsification conditions set before the runs were not triggered. Exp-01 showed the effect exists on one seed; Exp-02 shows the claim holds on all eleven — the frozen model never recovers. The specific 835-sample figure was seed luck and is retired. E01 supersedes the damage magnitudes: the legacy 294×/24× are upper bounds; the corrected gaps are ≈6.9× (damage_ref) and ≈10.8× (damage_full), and on the clean panel the worst DeepRiver seed is 0.74× the best frozen seed. The legacy worst-vs-best framing is retired. The one control expectation Exp-01 refuted (batch winning steady state) is restored by the larger sample, and streaming still wins the run outright.

docs.title: Roadmap v2 — DF-H, the deep hybrid detector
docs.text:
Approved: 2026-11-14 · Supersedes: the breadth-first E05–E15 detector plan. Existing results (E01–E17, KDD'26) stay; the detector track is now centred on one artefact.

The goal in one sentence: build DF-H, a detector that combines a label-free deep monitor with supervised confirmation, and make it beat the KDD'26 detector benchmark on its own protocol and win the delayed-label setting where error-only detectors are provably floor-bound.

Status update (2026-11-14): the E18 signal gate and the E19 v1 pilot both ran and failed their pre-registered gates. E18's best deep AUC was 0.616 vs the error rate's 0.598; E19's DF-H ranked 3rd (7.09) behind STEPD and SEED, with FAR below ADWIN but no primary feature-cell win. The full E20 matrix is not justified by the pilot-first rule. The feature monitor retains a real early-warning advantage on feature drift, and the Delay Tax benchmark (E21) is now the headline: the fixed-delay Lemma-1 synthesis shows Stage 1 warning at 70–513 samples vs 2,120–3,269 for the error-only panel at L = 2,000. The full regime matrix and Lemmas 2–3 are scaffolded but not run. E22 adds the focused capability check on the data in the repo: DF-H is 3rd overall (7.34), ahead of HDDM-W, ADWIN, HDDM-A and PageHinkley, and behind only SEED/STEPD; it owns feature permutation with a 0.04 FAR. See E18, E19, E21 and E22.

docs.title: 1. Why the goal changed
docs.text:
The last two months of evidence point to the same conclusion: no scalar detector wins everywhere, and the missing information is in the features, not in another error-stream vote.

Evidence What it says E04 — synthetic detector map HDDM-A is the best default on the static host for all four shapes, but recurring drift is only F1 0.500. E17 — real Elec2 The default is host-conditional: HDDM-A wins all four on the static HT, but ADWIN wins abrupt 1.000 vs 0.400 and recurring 0.770 vs 0.593 on the adaptive HAT. Best-host mean: ADWIN 0.935 vs HDDM-A 0.910. KDD'26 reproduction SEED/STEPD rank 2.12 (mean F1 0.300/0.303); HDDM-W 3.56; HDDM-A 3.87. The absolute ceiling is low — better signals matter. E02 — no-drift control Naive combinations are dangerous: EWMA makes ADWIN 0.548/1k and KSWIN 7.667/1k against a 0.1 target. ABCD(X) (cited) Feature-space detection is the strongest arm on feature permutation: rank 1.0 abrupt / 3.3 gradual. DriftFormer Already computes a masked-feature SSL loss and runs an internal ADWIN; forward() returns four head logits and the cls_out embedding. The detector is instrumentation + fusion, not a new model.

The target: SEED/STEPD at 2.12. DF-H does not need to win every cell; it needs to be top-2 overall and own the cells where feature information matters.

No scalar detector is universal. A feature monitor adds a different view, not another vote on the same error stream.

docs.title: 2. What DF-H is
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S["Stream x_t"] --> S1["Stage 1 — deep monitor<br/>SSL loss · embedding shift<br/>head disagreement · entropy"]
    S --> H["Host learner<br/>Hoeffding Tree / ARF"]
    H --> S2["Stage 2 — error-stream detectors<br/>SEED · STEPD · ADWIN · HDDM-A"]
    S1 -->|"warning"| F["Fusion<br/>calibrated, pre-registered"]
    S2 -->|"confirmation"| F
    F --> A["Reported alarm<br/>T_warn + T_confirm"]

Stage 1 watches the input stream without labels; Stage 2 confirms with the host's mistakes. The reported result has two times: warning and confirmation.

Stage Input Signals / detectors Labels needed? Stage 1 — deep monitor Raw features, frozen DriftFormer encoder SSL loss, embedding shift, head disagreement, entropy, internal ADWIN, feature-KS control No Stage 2 — confirmation Host mistake stream SEED, STEPD, ADWIN, HDDM-A on the raw channel Yes Fusion Both stages S1, S2, OR, AND, 2of3, 2of3_nodeep —

Stage 1 is the new information. It sees P(X) change directly, which is why it should win feature permutation/filtering and recurring change. Stage 2 keeps the cells where SEED/STEPD are strong, especially label swap and class-prior drift, where P(X) is unchanged and a label-free monitor has no power (Lemma 4).

docs.title: Fusion rules
docs.text:
Variant Rule Purpose S1 Stage 1 only Label-free ceiling; delay benchmark S2 Best fixed scalar detector The strong baseline OR Stage 1 or Stage 2 Earliest alarm; highest FAR risk AND Stage 1 and Stage 2 within W_confirm Precision-first 2of3 Stage 1 + SEED + ADWIN The candidate 2of3_nodeep SEED + ADWIN + HDDM-A Control: does deep add anything?

The final rule is pre-registered and calibrated to FAR ≤ 0.1/1k on E02 and the pre-drift 20% of each stream. No EWMA. No test-trial tuning.

docs.text: Criterion Bar Overall average rank top-2 (SEED/STEPD are at 2.12) Weak cells best on at least two of feature_permutation, feature_filtering, recurring False alarms FAR no worse than ADWIN Per-dataset robustness no dataset rank worse than 4 Stretch #1 overall

docs.text:
Criterion Bar Fixed delay L warning time grows by ≤ L + c; confirmation is floor-bound Partial labels higher recall than the best error-only detector at p = 0.5 and 0.1 Selective labels warn earlier on unlabelled drift; confirm when labels arrive Lemmas Lemma 1 (floor), Lemma 2 (1/√p), Lemma 3 (batch FAR) measured

docs.title: Milestone Report — Sept 9
docs.text:
Milestone summary: the project crosses from argument to measurement: the thesis is written down with pre-registered expectations, and the first atomic experiment (Exp-01) is run — it confirms the headline claim (a streaming deep learner recovers from drift in bounded time; a frozen batch model never does).

Date 2026-09-09 Focus Thesis written (Phase 0 → Phase 1) + Exp-01 first measured run Primary docs thesis.md · exp01-deepriver-vs-frozen-sea.md Data artifact experiments/exp01/results.json (repo root, next to the Exp-01 write-up)

docs.title: Why this milestone
docs.text: The project's promise — "take models that are not streaming and beat them on real metrics" — was, until today, an argument backed by other people's papers. A milestone needs a measured data point of our own. This report records the state after the first two deliverables: the thesis (the argument, with falsifiable pre-registered expectations) and Exp-01 (the first run of the pilot that the thesis was designed around).

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Thesis written (thesis.md) — the idea ("batch models update on a clock, streaming models on evidence"), the mechanism, the facts-with-sources it rests on, the expected event sequence, and §6f: what would falsify it. Every illustrative number is marked as pre-registered.
  • Exp-01 spec'd and run — one synthetic SEA stream, one abrupt drift at τ = 30,000, two models (DeepRiver rolling deep classifier, window 500, vs a frozen RandomForest), evaluated prequentially over 48,000 post-warm-up samples.
  • Exp-01 data + figures committed — experiments/exp01/results.json (per-sample rolling Kappa series + all metrics), rolling-Kappa curve and a damage-area summary chart in Phase1:Experimentation/figures/.
  • Environment hardened — Python pinned to 3.12 (deep-river's torch < 2.6 has no cp313 wheels), tool.uv.environments restricted to Linux + Apple-Silicon (the Intel-Mac torch wheel was the resolution blocker), GPU auto-detected (RTX 3050).
  • Repo home cleaned up — root README rewritten as the project-vision page; the docs index now reflects Phase 1 as running, not starting.

docs.title: Results — the numbers
docs.text:
Measured on seed 42, 60,000 samples (full series in experiments/exp01/results.json, next to the write-up):

Metric (post-warm-up, n = 48,000) DeepRiver rolling Frozen RF Cumulative accuracy 0.885 0.856 Cumulative Cohen Kappa 0.757 0.689 Pre-drift baseline κ₀ 0.755 0.759 Min rolling Kappa after drift 0.703 0.592 Recovery time (samples from τ) 835 never (stream ends first) Damage area (samples·κ) 31 3,307 DeepRiver loop runtime 99 s on RTX 3050 (484 samples/s) — (0.17 s fit)

Two headline behaviours, both as the thesis predicted:

Measured, not schematic: rolling Cohen Kappa (w = 1,000) over the stream, drift at τ = 30,000. Before the drift both models sit at ≈ 0.75 — equal skill. After it, the frozen RF falls to ≈ 0.59 and never returns; DeepRiver dips briefly and is back inside its pre-drift band 835 samples later.

docs.title: Pre-registration scorecard
docs.text:
The thesis's illustrative expectations (§6b, written before the run) vs what was measured:

Claim (pre-registered) Expected Measured Verdict Streaming recovery time is bounded ~250–350 samples (HAT/LB lines) 835 samples (DeepRiver, rolling window) PASS — same order of magnitude, inside the 5,000-sample falsification budget Frozen RF never recovers never never (still depressed at stream end) PASS Frozen pays unbounded damage unbounded 3,307 samples·κ vs 31 PASS (2 orders of magnitude) Frozen wins cumulative accuracy (H2, honest control) batch ahead in steady state DeepRiver wins 0.757 vs 0.689 REFUTED — streaming also wins the control; the pilot is stronger than pre-registered Dip depth streaming shallow, frozen deep 0.052 vs 0.167 PASS

docs.title: Issues faced & fixes
docs.text:
• Slow first run (~18 min CPU, 44 samples/s). The deep-river loop is per-sample windowed refit — genuinely expensive. Fixed by running the net on the RTX 3050: 99 s, ~11× faster (the script now auto-selects CUDA).
  • A memorisation confound in the stream. river 0.25's SEA reseeds its RNG per generator, so concatenating two concepts replayed the identical feature vectors under the new label rule — the frozen RF had literally seen its "test" chunk during warm-up (it crashed only where it had memorised flipped labels). Fixed by drawing one continuous feature stream and switching only the label rule at τ. Lesson: check generator internals before trusting a "synthetic" stream.
  • deep-river 0.3.4 bugs (two). utils.estimator_checks imports pytest at package import time (missing dep — added); and _learn runs the forward before module.train(), so cuDNN RNN backward crashes after a predict (worked around in the script). Documented in the exp01 write-up §2–3b.
  • The spec'd flattened MLP can't be a RollingClassifier — its feature handling requires the input layer to take n_features, so the module is a small RNN head (16 hidden), which is the architecture deep-river documents for rolling models.

docs.title: Status vs the plan
docs.text:
• The thesis's core falsifier is not triggered: streaming recovery (835) is bounded and ≪ any sane retrain interval; the frozen baseline's rolling Kappa did drop at drift (so there was real drift, not a dataset problem).
  • Honest limits of this milestone: single seed, synthetic stream, no drift detector yet, no scheduled-retrain baseline. The measured 835 samples came from a rolling window alone — the detection-delay component (d) is still untested, and the no-drift control experiment is pending.
  • The pipeline is now in place (data → artifact → figure → report), so the follow-ups are execution, not plumbing.

docs.title: Next milestone
docs.text:
1. Seed sweep (Exp-02): the same drift on ≥10 seeds → recovery time as a distribution (mean ± SD), not a single number.
  2. Baseline ladder: add scheduled-retrain batch (refit every k) and an oracle-tuned batch as the honest upper bound (Amekoe-style), so the frozen-only comparison broadens to the full thesis claim.
  3. Real streams (Elec2, Phishing, Covertype, Airlines, CreditCard) with the post-dip metric protocol.
  4. The Delay Tax experiment: label-delay sweep, where batch retraining starves and streaming must keep working on yesterday's labels.

docs.title: ABSTRACT
docs.text:
Problem. Conventional machine learning treats the training set as a finished object, whereas production data arrives as an unbounded stream whose generating process changes over time. A learner that updates per sample recovers from such a change, and a model trained once and frozen does not. Existing drift detectors, however, observe the error stream, and in fraud confirmation, advertising attribution and intrusion triage the labels that feed that stream arrive late. Label delay therefore imposes a floor on every error-based detector, and that floor has not been quantified at detector level.

Methodology. A config-driven experiment harness, DriftLab, was built on River 0.25.0, DeepRiver 0.3.4 and PyTorch 2.5.1, with prequential (test-then-train) evaluation and a fixed-window damage metric anchored to a panel-shared pre-drift reference. Eleven experiments cover streaming against frozen and scheduled batch learners, synthetic and real detector maps, a 2,800-task reproduction of the KDD'26 detector benchmark, a deep signal gate, a rule-based fusion detector named DF-H, and a fixed-delay synthesis of the label tax.

Key Results. The corrected fixed-window damage is 74.8 against 515.0 samples times kappa, approximately 6.9 times lower for the streaming learner, with frozen recovery on 0 of 11 seeds. The KDD'26 ranking is reproduced with SEED and STEPD tied first at 2.12 and HDDM-A fourth at 3.87. DF-H ranks third overall at 7.34 behind STEPD and SEED, with a false-alarm rate of 0.04 per 1,000 samples and a clear win on feature permutation. At a delay of 2,000 samples the label-free warning fires in 70 to 513 samples against 2,120 to 3,269 for the error-only panel. The pre-registered top-2 gate and the deep signal gate both fail and are reported as failures.

Societal Relevance. The work supports reliable adaptation in fraud detection, intrusion monitoring and credit risk, where silent degradation harms users. Bounded-memory learning reduces repeated full retraining, and the negative results are reported rather than hidden.

docs.title: 1.1 Background
docs.text:
Machine learning is usually taught on a finished dataset that is loaded, split, trained on and then treated as complete. Production data is not finished. It arrives one sample at a time, potentially without end, and is often too large or too fast to store. Three constraints define a genuine streaming algorithm: a single pass, memory that does not grow with the number of samples, and a bounded processing time per sample [4], [13], [25].

The distribution that generates the stream does not stay fixed. Concept drift is a change in the joint distribution of features and labels over time, and it appears in four recognised shapes: abrupt, gradual, incremental and recurring [3], [4]. A model trained once and deployed is blind to all four. A model that updates on every sample can follow the change, because its own error signal is evidence that the world has moved [5], [11], [19].

Most detectors in the field watch that error signal, which means they consume labels. In fraud confirmation, advertising attribution and intrusion triage the labels arrive hours or days later, so every error-based detector inherits a floor equal to the delay. This report treats that floor as a measurable quantity, calls it the Delay Tax, and builds a detector that escapes it where the input distribution moves.

docs.title: 1.2 Problem Definition and Objectives
docs.text:
The technical problem separates two questions that the literature usually conflates. The first is whether continual learning pays: does a learner that updates per sample recover from a concept change, and how much damage does it avoid relative to a model trained once or retrained on a clock. The second is whether drift can be detected before labels arrive, and which drift types permit it.

Five measurable objectives were set for the work.

  • O1. Demonstrate at least a five times lower fixed-window damage for a streaming learner against a frozen learner over at least ten seeds, with zero frozen recoveries.
  • O2. Map classical detector performance across four drift shapes and two hosts, and reproduce the published KDD'26 detector ranking.
  • O3. Design and evaluate DF-H on an 80-cell pilot with a false-alarm rate at or below 0.1 per 1,000 samples and an overall rank in the top three, while reporting the top-2 gate honestly.
  • O4. Quantify the Delay Tax at a fixed delay of 2,000 samples and show a label-free Stage 1 warning at least twice as early as the best error-only detector.
  • O5. Deliver a reproducible harness with saved artifacts and automated tests for every reported number.

docs.title: 1.3 Social and Environmental Relevance
docs.text:
Fraud detection, intrusion monitoring and credit risk scoring share a property that makes this work consequential: the model's output decides something about a person, and the label that would correct the model arrives much later. Silent degradation produces false approvals, missed fraud and unfairly persistent decisions against groups affected by a distributional change.

Single-pass learning with bounded memory also has an environmental reading. A model that updates incrementally does not re-read the historical corpus on a schedule, so the compute, storage and energy of repeated full retraining are avoided, and retention of raw history is no longer required for correctness.

docs.text: The work was organised as ten work packages across seven relative phases, labelled relatively rather than by calendar date so that the plan stays readable independently of the academic timetable.

The seven phases follow one another in the order shown in Table 1.1, with the literature, harness and pilot phases overlapping the start phase. The Gantt chart in Figure 1.1 carries the same seven labels on a relative week axis. Scheduled retrain intervals, by contrast, are a property of the models under test rather than of the project, and they are reported in samples throughout.

Figure 1.1: Project timeline by phase. Seven phases are placed on a relative week axis from week 1 to week 12, with no calendar dates. The start, literature review and harness phases overlap the opening weeks, the pilot runs into the middle of the schedule, the mid review sits at its close, and result accumulation precedes the final report.

docs.title: 1.5 Scope and Limitations
docs.text:
The work covers classification on drifting streams, implemented in River and DeepRiver, evaluated prequentially over synthetic generators and public real streams, at detector level and at model level. It includes a two-stage detector, a fixed-delay synthesis of the label tax, and a reproducible artifact pipeline.

It excludes regression, clustering and recommendation, distributed or federated training, a production service, and novel deep architectures. The stochastic, partial, selective and batch delay matrix is implemented but not benchmarked, and the ABCD and ABCD(X) arm of the benchmark is cited rather than reproduced.

docs.title: CHAPTER 2: LITERATURE SURVEY AND CRITICAL REVIEW
2.1 Critical Review
docs.text:
Foundations and evaluation. Streaming learning rests on a small set of uncontested results. Domingos and Hulten showed that a decision tree can be grown in one pass with constant memory per leaf [4]. Bifet and Gavalda supplied the adaptive window that most of the field still uses, with a false-positive guarantee that made detector evaluation quantitative [8], [9]. Gama, Sebastiao and Rodrigues formalised prequential scoring, in which each sample is predicted before it trains the model [11]. River packaged these primitives into a Python ecosystem [13], and DeepRiver extended the same interface to PyTorch learners [22].

Detector benchmarking and host dependence. The detector literature is long and, read carefully, negative. Gama et al. introduced DDM as statistical process control on the error stream [5], Baena-Garcia et al. added EDDM to catch gradual change through the distance between errors [6], and Page's cumulative sum scheme [1], given its minimax formulation by Lorden [2], survives as Page-Hinkley. Each method reports a win on its own evaluation, and the comparisons do not agree. Goncalves et al. summarised the position in 2014: no detector dominates on delay, false alarms and misses at once. Cerqueira et al. converted that folk result into a proper benchmark, with seven real datasets, four injected drift types, two transition speeds and a timing-aware F1 detection score [27]. Their ranking places SEED and STEPD first, with HDDM-A mid-table.

The benchmark also exposes an unexamined variable. A detector watches the mistakes of a specific host learner, and the host adapts while the detector is watching. A one-sided test such as HDDM-A can therefore miss a change that an adaptive host repairs before the test separates. This report treats host dependence as a first-class measurement and reports detector maps on both a static and an adaptive host.

Delayed and partial labels. Zliobaite asked the question that governs this area: when a change arrives with delayed labelling, is it detectable at all [10]. The answer is conditional. Pure posterior drift, in which the conditional distribution of the label given the features changes while the feature distribution does not, leaves no trace in the input stream, so no label-free method can see it. Grzenda, Gomes and Bifet supplied the evaluation protocol for the delayed case [12]. Gomes et al. surveyed semi-supervised learning for delayed partially labelled streams and named the delayed and partial intersection as under-explored [16]. Botacin and Gomes measured the operational cost in a malware pipeline, reporting roughly a 50 percent increase in user exposure and a decrease of up to 75 percent in detection as delay grows [20]. Alencar et al. confirmed that the terminology itself is fragmented [24].

Label-free and hybrid detection. STUDD detects drift without labels by monitoring how well a student model imitates the deployed teacher [18], and it demonstrates both the value and the limit of the approach: it works when the input distribution moves, and it fails on pure posterior drift, exactly as Zliobaite predicted [10], [18]. The active-learning line attacks the same problem from the acquisition side [15]. Agu et al. gate deep adaptation on a parametric detector, which is architecturally close to the two-stage idea but sidesteps delayed ground truth by using pseudo-labels [23]. Applied work adds the operational case: Hans and Zuhlke show an online ensemble beating weekly batch retraining [25], Abdoune et al. compare iterative batch against incremental learning on a digital twin [26], and Carneiro et al. predict whether retraining will help before spending the compute [14]. Imbalanced drifting streams are where adaptive ensembles have the strongest published record, with ROSE reporting a mean kappa of 63.65 against 57.85 for the next-best of thirty ensembles over twenty-four real datasets [17].

The open position. Three results run through the review. Detector quality is host-conditional, so a detector claim without a host is incomplete. Label-free monitoring is limited to changes that leave a trace in the input distribution. An immediate-label benchmark now exists, and the equivalent for delayed, partial and selective labels does not. No logged paper builds and evaluates a two-stage warning and confirmation protocol against a calibrated detector panel, which is the gap this project occupies [16], [18].
